{"method":"get_file","path":"CLAUDE.md","content":"# OrcaSlicer AI Redesign — Locked Decisions & Lessons

## ⚠ LESSON: the agent chat is a full, visible conversation — NEVER a one-line input
The user↔agent interaction is messy, multi-turn, back-and-forth, and often NOT cleanly
summarizable. ALWAYS show the ENTIRE chat history as a real scrollable conversation (the
dock), with the settled "Current setup" plan PINNED at the top as the artifact. Do NOT
collapse the conversation into a single input field, a one-line "refine…" box, or a tidy
changelog. The pinned plan is the source of truth for what will slice; the thread below it
is disposable exploration that stays fully visible. (Decided turns 3–4; regressed in turn 6.
Do not repeat.)

## Core conceptual model
- One app = a slicer. Home shows TWO concepts: **Projects** (your work; opens the Prepare
  screen) and **Printers** (your equipment: connection, model, filament/AMS colours,
  calibration, and a **Launch monitor** button). The monitor is a sub-window launched from a
  printer — never a co-equal app.
- Navigation = model **A**: one main window that navigates Home ⇄ Prepare/Check (+ Info) ⇄
  Printer config. Only monitor windows pop out (one per printer, many at once). Opening a
  second project REPLACES the first in the main window; you switch projects via Home. The
  ORCA logo / back control top-left returns to Home; projects auto-save.
- Ownership boundary: the USER supplies what is physically true, what the geometry MEANS, and
  the desired OUTCOME, and holds authority over consequential physical actions. The AGENT owns
  the ~247 invisible process settings (layers, walls, infill, speed, cooling, supports, seams…).
- Printer/filament/colour/model are FACTS ABOUT THE MACHINE → they live in Printer config. The
  project just POINTS at a printer via a loose picker (default: last-used / whatever's idle;
  changeable anytime, never a required first step). Colour INVENTORY = printer; colour→region
  MAPPING = project.
- Painting = annotate MEANING ("smooth face", "bearing surface", "screw hole", "no supports
  here"), and the agent DERIVES the modifiers — not user-set local wall counts / speeds.
- App-level presets/profiles/materials SHIP with the app; most users never touch them. They are
  discoverable only behind the "see all" door, when presets aren't enough. Do not give them
  prime real estate (fold into Preferences).

## Prepare-screen design principles
1. The agent is a SECOND input path, so every visible tool is an OPTIONAL accelerator — anything
   a tool does, you can also just ask for. Beginners talk; makers grab the tool.
2. The conversation is ALWAYS visible (see the lesson above): full history + pinned plan.
3. Four fixed zones, learned once: machine (top) · object on the plate (centre) · intent+plan
   conversation dock (right) · the one commit button, Slice (bottom).
4. Words/outcomes on the surface; numbers/parameters one "see all" layer down.
5. Depth opens as a dismissible layer over/beside the current context; the standing screen never
   permanently accumulates.

## Screen inventory
- **Home** — Projects + Printers.
- **Project window** (one main window, model A) with modes: **Prepare** (plate + tools + dock),
  **Check/Preview** (sliced paths, layer scrub, time/material, risks), **Info** (project
  knowledge: author, licence, safety, BOM, assembly, pictures, versions).
- **Printer config** — sections: Setup · Filament/AMS · Calibration · Maintenance & Privacy.
- **Monitor window** — pop-out per printer: camera, progress, temps, Pause/Resume/Stop, alerts.
- **Dialogs / overlays**: Send (preflight, one-way), the "see all" expert-settings layer,
  Preferences (app-level: cloud, offline, network, updates, presets/materials library).

## Agent setup (decided turn 9–10)
- "Set up the agent" opens a **layer over the dock** (9c) — not a modal, not a chat. One primary
  path (Continue with JusPrin) + a quiet door for the expert paths (own API key · local model via
  JusPrin MCP server). The same sheet is Preferences › Agent. Nothing from setup enters the thread
  or the .3mf.
- Sign-in is a **browser hand-off** (10a–c): Orca waits with Copy link / Enter code hatches; the
  done page always shows the code; on return the layer closes into the first chat with a
  dismissible, unsaved "Connected · who" strip. Connecting creates no card.
- Changing it later (11): the dock's chat ▾ menu carries one last line (dot · path · who) that
  opens the SAME 9c sheet in a connected state (status block + Sign out, plan/quota here only,
  Switch-to door, quiet "Turn the agent off"). Preferences › Agent is that sheet verbatim. When the
  agent breaks, a red unsaved line takes the Connected strip's slot with the fix for that failure;
  plan, thread and Slice are untouched. No agent avatar in the top bar, no gear in the dock header.

## Connect AI tools (decided turn 14) — replaces the "model on this machine" path in 9d
- Direction: Orca IS the MCP server; an AI app the user already runs (Claude Code, Codex, Claude
  Desktop, Cowork local sessions, Cursor, VS Code) connects to the open project. Door in 9c reads
  "Connect an AI tool you already use"; same sheet at Preferences › Connect AI tools. Not a login,
  not a chat, adds no agent to the dock (its proposals wait for approval in the Agent panel).
- User decides two things only: which app · save settings automatically or Copy for manual setup.
  Never types URL/port/key/token/server name. "Detected" = executable or config file found, nothing
  more; undetected apps stay selectable.
- Steps: Choose app → Prepare (generated command/config, Connect… · Copy · Close) → Review (verbatim
  permission question + exact change: command, or file path + old/new entry, others preserved, backup
  made; Cancel is default) → Saving (no Cancel; backend can't interrupt) → "Configuration saved.
  Restart the client to load JusPrin." + backup path. Manual: "Copied. No client settings were
  changed." NEVER say "Connected" — nothing is tested.
- Errors, one at a time, each with its fix: helper missing · client CLI missing · config
  invalid/unwritable · changed since preview → review again · command failed (folded technical
  output) · timeout "settings might have changed; inspect before retrying". Advanced/developer
  details collapsed (local address, server start-up error). No disconnect/test/auto-restart (not built).
- Wireframes: `Orca Agent Wireframes 2.dc.html` (turn 14+).

## Prepare header & pinned card (decided turn 12)
- ONE job button, right side of the header, above the dock: Slice ▾ → (Slicing…) → Check print ▾ /
  Print ▾. Slice and Print are mutually exclusive in OrcaSlicer's code (Slice disabled while the
  plate's slice result is valid; Print enabled only then), so they never coexist. Check print shares
  the sliced state with Print: primary when the agent flagged something, otherwise in the ▾ menu.
  Multi-plate: "Print plate 2 ▾", menu has Slice/Print all plates + Export sliced file. Print always
  opens Send preflight.
- Printer chip = printer nickname · nozzle · plate · loaded spools as dots IN SLOT ORDER (never the
  project palette). Capped width, full names on hover. Mismatch = chip turns red and shows only the
  offending fact + inline fix; it's the only red thing in the header.
- Pinned card = YOU WANT (user's words, editable) · PLAN (agent's derived setup) · "Ready to check"
  until a valid slice exists, then time · material. No risk line on the card (dropped as too hard).
- No permanent toolbar: handles + strip (Place on face · Duplicate · Mark ▾ · ⋯) on selection only;
  ⋯ = mirror, cut, split, merge, text, measure, repair. Plate label at the plate's front edge shows
  what's on it and the colours used. Objects rail opens into a tree only when >1 object/plate/colour.
- Header = three zones: ‹ Home (left; no ORCA wordmark) · printer chip CENTRED · job button + ⋯ (right). No
  "Prints · x" chip in the header — print history lives on Home and in ⋯.
- Project name lives in the window title (Mac/Win); Linux shows it after Home. No dirty indicator.
- SUPERSEDED by turn 15 (below) — Printer chip click (turn 13) = popover, ~300px: a list of printers, one card each, EVERY card with
  its own settings ⚙ and monitor ↗ doors (never a shared door at the bottom). Chosen card expanded:
  full names · LOADED one row per slot in slot order ("used" marks the project's slots, ? = unknown
  spool, colour is a swatch only — printer sends hex not a name; remain % only for tagged Bambu
  spools). Others collapsed with status; click body to switch. "+ Add a printer" last. Non-Bambu
  printers have no live data: show configured values labelled "as set up". Read-only; no colour→slot
  mapping here. Red state adds a top block with the
  mismatch + two fixes; one mismatch at a time, worst first (offline > nozzle > plate > filament).
- Wireframes for this: `Orca Prepare Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 12+).

## Printer + spool chip (decided turn 15) — replaces the turn-12 chip and turn-13 popover
- ONE chip, TWO halves, parent → child: left = printer nickname · nozzle; right (nested, lighter
  ground, same outline) = colour dot · spool name. No plate on the chip. Slot dots only when the
  printer has slots (AMS / MMU). The chip NEVER turns red — it states facts; mismatches go to the
  thread + pinned card status row (retires 12c's red chip). Hover lifts one half and shows full names.
- Spool menu (right half): title "SPOOLS ON <printer>"; spools the person has used on this printer,
  last-used order, current ✓; click row = swapped, closes (2 clicks). Rare actions (change colour,
  rename, tune with the agent, reset tuning, filament settings, remove) only via ⋯ on hover/right-click.
  Last row "Other spool…" = search every preset that fits printer+nozzle → colour pick → prefilled
  name → "Use this spool" (adds to list). Quiet escapes: Generic preset… · Import a preset file….
- Printer menu (left half), one-printer = 5 lines: name + state (dot + word; ↗ monitor when connected)
  · Nozzle ▸ · Plate ▸ · Printer settings… · Add a printer…. Not connected shows one grey sub-line
  ("Prints go to a card. Connect…"). Multi-printer adds ONE middle section "OTHER PRINTERS" (state,
  ⚙ ↗ per row, click = switch). No fleet UI for one-printer people.
- Add a printer = 3 questions: 1 brand · model · nozzle (everyone's path; network finds listed under it
  as a shortcut — Bambu only via SSDP — picking one prefills the model and asks for the LAN access code
  or sign-in) · 2 plate · 3 "What spool is on it right now?" (same picker). Row clicks advance; Next
  only where several fields exist. Klipper/Moonraker/PrusaLink addresses go in later via the printer
  menu's Connect…. No filament page.
- AMS chip label = what the project prints with (✓ row), never slot 1: one spool → its name; several →
  "N spools", every used slot dot ringed.
- AMS: spool half = chosen spool name + slot dots; menu top section = slots as reported (swatch, plastic,
  % for tagged Bambu only; Unknown → Identify…); remembered spools below. Klipper MMU: same, from the
  gate map, footer says so, no %. After a swap: chip, PLAN material word, one grey system line in the
  thread; the chat never changes the selection.
- Tokens: JusPrin light/dark set (from the brief) applies at hi-fi; wireframes stay lo-fi.

## Printer conversation placement (turn 19 — EXPLORATION, undecided)
- VOCABULARY (user asked): "conversation panel" = the Prepare-screen agent column (thread + input,
  pinned card where one applies), attached to the window edge, never a modal. "printers column" = the
  PRINTERS strip on Home (5b). Avoid the coined words "dock" and "cabinet" in labels from now on.
- Six placements for a freeform printer thread (Add + Change), each with a pinned facts card unless the
  UI itself is the artifact: 19a modal chat · 19b printers column becomes the conversation panel · 19c
  main window navigates to Printer config with a conversation panel (config page = the artifact, no
  pinned card) · 19d permanent conversation panel on Home, cards carry state · 19e printer card expands
  into its own thread · 19f = 18b first, correction field grows into a thread on demand. Agent lean:
  19c (+19f's reveal).
- Thread rules (Ken, turn 19 comments): every opening is a NEW session (no carried history); the AGENT
  opens the thread saying what it can do here; chips are specific actions ("Use 0.3 mm layers"), never
  bare Yes/No, and the open input always sits beneath them; a panel header label names where ‹ leads
  ("Printers"), not the current item.
- 19b·Add (Ken): the Add flow in the panel must carry ALL of 18's information in chat form: opener lists
  words / photo / network finds in the FIRST agent message; camera icon in the input row on every screen;
  recognised = 18b card + assumptions line + "Add this printer" primary chip; ambiguous = 18d; network
  = 18c. Photo upload must be discoverable and possible in every thread: a LABELLED "Photo" button LEADS the
  composer (leading-edge attach, as chat apps do, but labelled because it's a primary path), whole panel is
  a drop zone; a photo never auto-sends — removable thumbnail above the composer, optional words, explicit
  send (thumbnail INSIDE the composer box, above the text line); the sent photo shows in the thread as the
  user's message. No dashed drop card (looked like a candidate card, vanished after turn one): the agent's
  opener says how in words. Composer placeholders are a likely ANSWER to the agent's last message; on the first
  turn that is an example answer to the opener ("e.g. bambu a1 mini or not sure, the small one"), never
  "type…". The photo path is a separate, styled TIP paragraph under the opener (red left rule, camera). Primary chips = chip shape, red fill.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 19.

## Add a printer (decided turn 18; 16 and 17 REJECTED — no chat window, no pinned card)
- LESSON: don't convert wizard steps into a chat. The agent's value is (a) recognising the printer
  from ANY evidence — loose words, a dropped photo of the printer/nameplate/box, or what the network
  reports — and (b) knowing what NOT to ask: nozzle/plate/filament get stated defaults, corrected
  later in the Prepare chip (15a) or the project conversation. Setup settles ONE fact.
- Home = 5b. "+ Add printer" → small dialog: "What printer do you have?" free-text field + drop-a-photo
  + FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK rows ("Use this") + small link "Set it up myself" (ConfigWizard, unchanged).
- Recognised → ONE card (profile picture + name) + one line "I'll assume 0.4 mm nozzle, the textured
  PEI plate it ships with, and PLA. If different, tell me here or in your first project" + one
  correction field + Not this one / Add this printer. Correction redraws the card; no thread.
- "Use this" on a network find (Bambu SSDP, Klipper/PrusaLink mDNS) → the SAME 18b screen, card
  filled from what the printer reported (nozzle, plate, AMS slots); sentence says nothing is assumed;
  one optional access-code field; Not this one / Add this printer (Add connects when a code is given).
- Ambiguous words → the agent states what tells the candidates apart, shows 2–3 picture cards, offers
  a photo as the shortcut, and KEEPS the text field (tap, photo or more words all answer); "not in the
  list" → wizard custom-printer page, prefilled.
- After Add: cabinet card on top ("as set up"/connected) + dismissable STARTER MODELS row.
- Manual path (18e) = "Set it up myself" link in 18a or "not in the list" in 18d → the dialog body
  becomes the existing ConfigWizard printer page, unchanged, with a header link "Ask the agent
  instead"; whatever the agent inferred is pre-ticked.
- No agent set up (18f) = 18a's layout with the text field replaced by 8a's connect card (title "No
  agent connected" · one-sentence nudge about THIS screen only · red "Set up the agent" → 9c ·
  sub-line; no disabled input).
  Network finds and "set it up myself" still work without an agent; on return the dialog becomes 18a.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 18; 17 kept dimmed for reference).

## Add a printer (turn 17 — REJECTED, kept for history)
- Home = 5b (projects gallery + printer cabinet). "+ Add printer" opens a MODAL DIALOG over Home with
  ONE question: "Let the agent guide me" (leads) · "Set it up myself". The pick REPLACES the dialog body
  in place: agent → a chat window (header link "Set it up myself instead" · ×; PINNED "New printer"
  card Printer · Nozzle · Plate · Filament shown empty up front, fills as facts settle; thread beneath;
  one input); self → OrcaSlicer's existing ConfigWizard printer dialog UNCHANGED (vendor, model grid
  with pictures + nozzle ticks, Filaments, Bed shape/Firmware for custom; Back/Next/Finish) plus a
  header link "Ask the agent instead". Switching either way carries settled facts; never asked twice.
  No agent set up → agent card greyed "Set up the agent first" (9c), form card leads. Never turn the
  cabinet column into a panel.
- Questions in order, each with its default as the first (bold) tap chip: which printer (words →
  profile match → picture card "This one?"; 2–3 fits → 2–3 cards; "I don't know" → where to look +
  brand chips; not in list → custom profile, bed then firmware, one question at a time, pinned card
  swaps rows) → nozzle ("Most printers ship with 0.4. Did you change it?", only sizes that exist) →
  filament ("Most people start with PLA", brand/colour optional, mapped to a shipped profile else
  Generic) → plate (only if the profile lists >1) → confirm line = pinned card read aloud → Done.
  Settled facts appear as grey ✓ lines in the thread. Connecting is NOT part of setup (printer menu's
  Connect…); the panel says so once.
- Done closes the dialog → cabinet shows the new card on top ("as set up", Connect… link) and a
  dismissable STARTER MODELS row for that printer above the projects; opening one = new project → Prepare.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 17+).

## Visual system
Modernist design system (flat, Archivo, red #ec3013 on light, 2px rules, 0 radius). The working
files are LO-FI wireframes (Kalam sketch font) — options canvases, newest turn on top, ids like
6a/6b. `Orca Home Wireframes.dc.html` holds turns 1–6; `Orca Agent Wireframes.dc.html` holds 7–11
(dock, unconfigured state, agent setup and after); `Orca Agent Wireframes 2.dc.html` holds 14+. Start a new page when one grows past ~5 turns.
Hi-fi in Modernist comes later.

Yes, I understand what needs to be done. On Home, the printers column stops opening a pop-up dialog. Instead, the column itself turns into a chat panel, the same kind as the agent panel on the Prepare screen, both when you add a printer and when you click an existing printer card. The current look stays; only the layout and flow change. Four decisions below change how much gets built, so I need your answers before I start.

## What the design asks for

**The panel (both flows)**
- The printers column on Home swaps for the chat panel, and the projects stay visible on the left. The header has "‹ Printers" to go back to the list and a "Set it up myself" link.
- A card pinned at the top has four rows: Printer, Nozzle, Plate and Filament. Values are tagged "assumed" or "changed" where that applies.
- Below it is the chat history. Every opening starts a fresh session, and the agent speaks first to say what it can do here.
- Suggested replies are specific actions such as "Use 0.3 mm layers", never bare Yes/No. The main action is filled red, and the text box always sits under the suggestions.
- The text box has a labelled **Photo** button at its left edge, and you can drop a photo anywhere on the panel. A photo shows as a removable thumbnail inside the text box and is only sent when you press send. After sending, it appears in the chat as your message.
- The text box's placeholder is a likely answer to the agent's last message, e.g. "bambu a1 mini" or "not sure, the small one".

**Adding a printer ("+ Add printer")** carries over everything the current dialog does, as chat:
- **Opening message:** "What printer do you have?", a highlighted tip about using a photo, and a "Found on your network" list with "Use this" buttons.
- **Printer recognised:** a card with the printer's picture and the line "I'll assume 0.4 mm nozzle, textured PEI, PLA…". The pinned card fills in with "assumed" values. Suggestions are **Add this printer** and **Not this one**.
- **Several possible matches:** the agent says what tells them apart and shows two picture cards, each with a "This one" button, plus "Neither · not in the list" and a suggestion to send a photo.
- **After "Use this" on a network printer:** nothing is assumed, because the printer reported its own setup. The text box asks for the access code, which is optional, and there's a "sign in to Bambu" link.
- **Photo:** the agent answers the photo with the recognised card.

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, approval and verification requirements.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and authorization of consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

# Handoff: the printer conversation panel on Home (wireframe 19b)

Status: approved for implementation by Kenneth on 2026-09-17. Nothing is built yet.

Today "+ Add printer" on Home opens a native modal dialog (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/`) that runs a fixed recognition script against OpenAI. This work deletes that dialog. Instead, Home's printers column turns into an agent conversation panel, the same shape as the Prepare-screen agent column, and the real agent handles both **adding** a printer and **changing** an existing one. Visual styling stays exactly as it is in the app today; only the layout, flow, copy and behaviour come from the wireframes.

Paths below are relative to the repo root. `J/` means `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

---

## 1. Design sources (read these first)

Claude Design project `d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e`
(https://claude.ai/design/p/d981c5e2-20db-445f-9047-fa9e9a12522e). Read it through the DesignSync tool (`list_files` / `get_file`).

| File in the design project | What to read |
| --- | --- |
| `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` | Turn 19. Element `id="19b"`: the **Change** flow, a printer's conversation on Home. Element `id="19b-add"`: the **Add** flow, six panel states left to right. Also read turn 18 (`18a`–`18f`): 19b-add must carry all of 18's information, and 18e/18f describe "Set it up myself" and the no-agent state. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | The design's decision log. Read the sections "Printer conversation placement (turn 19)", "Add a printer (decided turn 18)", "Agent setup (decided turn 9–10)" and "Connect AI tools (turn 14)". Section 19 is marked "EXPLORATION, undecided"; Kenneth has since picked 19b, so this document overrides that label. |
| `support.js` | The runtime that renders `.dc.html` files. To view the wireframes, save both files into one folder and serve it over HTTP (for example `python3 -m http.server`), then open `wf.html#19b`. A `file://` URL does not work. Use a viewport of at least 1400 px. |

### How to read "pixel-perfect" here

The wireframes are deliberately **lo-fi**: Kalam sketch font, beige palette, and a 660 px frame in which the panel is 250 px wide. Do not copy their colours, fonts or pixel sizes. Match these exactly:

- the **structure and order** of every element in each panel state;
- the **relative emphasis**: which chip is filled, which value is muted, which text is red;
- the **copy**, word for word (quoted in section 3);
- the **behaviour** in the captions (section 3).

Take every colour, radius, font and control size from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: a value with no token gets a token and a guard first. Where the wireframe uses an element the app already has, reuse that element's current look:

| Wireframe class (in the `.dc.html` `<style>` block) | Existing app element to reuse |
| --- | --- |
| `.dlg-h` panel header | `J/AgentUI/src/components/ChatNavigation.tsx` |
| `.pin` pinned card, `.kv` rows | `J/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx` and its `pinned-setup` band (`J/AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, near line 392) |
| `.abub` agent message, `.ubub` user message | `J/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx` / `MarkdownMessage.tsx` |
| `.inp` composer, staged photo | `J/AgentUI/src/components/Composer.tsx`, `AttachmentChip.tsx` |
| `.pc` printer card with picture | New. Base it on Home's `J/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx` surface tokens. |
| `.opt` chip, `.opt.def` suggested chip, `.go` primary chip | New suggestion-chip row. Use existing button recipes (`--button-<recipe>-padding`) and the chip radius token. |

Panel width: the wireframe's 250 px is a proportion of a 660 px sketch, not a size. Use the existing Home printers-column token (`--printer-card-column-width`, 320 in `design-tokens.json` today) unless Kenneth says otherwise. The wireframe itself notes that the column is tight for picture cards, so check the ambiguous state (two picture cards) at that width.

---

## 2. Decisions already made (do not re-ask)

1. **Placement is 19b.** Home's printers column is replaced in place by the conversation panel. The projects gallery on the left stays visible. "‹ Printers" in the panel header returns to the printer list.
2. **Add is an open conversation with the real in-app agent**, not the old `PrinterSetupController` state machine and not the direct `OpenAIPrinterRecognition` call. Delete both.
3. **Change is in scope.** A printer's "Printer settings…" (the `…` menu on a Home printer card) opens this panel for that printer instead of OrcaSlicer's settings window.
4. **"Printer settings…" in the Prepare header's printer menu** (`J/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp`, around line 105) also goes to Home and opens the same panel for the current printer.
5. **"Set it up myself"** in the panel header:
   - Add flow: opens OrcaSlicer's ConfigWizard printer page, unchanged. This is what `run_manual_setup` in `J/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp` does today; keep that behaviour when you delete the file.
   - Change flow: opens OrcaSlicer's existing printer settings window, which is what "Printer settings…" did before (`Printers::open_named_printer_settings` → `SetupCommands::open_settings_tab(TYPE_PRINTER)`).
6. **Delete the old native dialog** and its tests (see section 5).
7. **No agent set up:** the panel shows the same agent-setup page and flow the old dialog embedded: a throwaway `AgentWebView` loaded with `?embedded=1`. When setup finishes, the panel switches to the conversation.
8. **An external AI tool is connected instead of an in-app agent** (the "Connect an AI tool" / MCP path, where the model runs in Claude Code, Cursor and so on): the Home panel has no in-app agent to talk to, so it shows the agent-setup page, the same as decision 7.
9. **Leave out the re-slice claim.** The 19b Change wireframe's agent reply says "Your two projects on this printer will re-slice with it next time you open them." Nothing implements that, so the agent must not say it.

---

## 3. Screen specification

### 3.1 Panel anatomy (every state)

From top to bottom:

1. **Header**:
   - left: `‹` then the label **"Printers"** (the label names where ‹ leads, not the current printer);
   - right: the link **"Set it up myself"**.
   - There is no close ×; ‹ is the way out.
2. **Pinned card**:
   - a small uppercase caption, **"NEW PRINTER"** (Add) or **"PRINTER"** (Change);
   - four label/value rows: **Printer · Nozzle · Plate · Filament**.
   - Each value has one of four styles:
     - *empty*: an em dash `—` in the most muted text colour;
     - *settled*: normal weight-600 text;
     - *assumed*: regular-weight secondary text with the suffix ` · assumed`;
     - *changed*: accent/red text with the suffix ` · changed`.
   - The Filament value can include a colour swatch (see the "Use this" state).
3. **Thread**: the full conversation, scrollable. Agent messages are plain text with no bubble. User messages are right-aligned bubbles. Cards, tip boxes and chip rows sit inline in the thread.
4. **Composer**, pinned to the bottom, with an accent border:
   - It starts with a **labelled "Photo" button** (camera icon plus the word "Photo"), on every screen.
   - Then the text line. Its placeholder is a likely *answer* to the agent's last message (quoted per state below), never "Type a message…".
   - A staged photo sits **inside** the composer box, above the text line: a 48 px-class square thumbnail with a × to remove it, and beside it the file name plus the hint "add a note, or just send". Then the Photo button, the typed text and a round accent send button (↑).
5. **The whole panel is a drop zone** for images. Dropping or choosing a photo never sends it; sending is always explicit.

Thread rules (from the design's CLAUDE.md, Kenneth's comments on turn 19):
- Every opening is a **new session**. No history carries over, and nothing is saved into the project `.3mf`.
- The **agent speaks first**, saying what it can do here.
- Suggestion chips are **specific actions** ("Use 0.3 mm layers"), never bare Yes/No. The open composer always sits beneath them, and a muted hint "or just type" may follow the chips.
- The **primary chip** has the same chip shape as the others and differs only by accent fill.

### 3.2 Change flow (`#19b`)

Entry: "Printer settings…" on a Home printer card, or in the Prepare header's printer menu (which first navigates to Home).

Wireframe example, for a Bambu Lab A1 Combo:

- Pinned card, caption "PRINTER":
  - Printer `Bambu Lab A1 Combo`
  - Nozzle `0.6 mm · changed` (red)
  - Plate `Textured PEI` (assumed style, no suffix)
  - Filament `AMS · 4 slots`
- Agent opener: "This is the A1 Combo. Tell me what changed on it, or ask anything about it: nozzle, plate, spools, connection. A photo of the part works too."
- User: "i put a 0.6 nozzle on it"
- Agent: "Changed to 0.6 mm. With 0.6 you can also print thicker layers." The wireframe's re-slice sentence is dropped (decision 9).
- Chips: **"Use 0.3 mm layers"** (suggested style: dark outline, bold) · "Keep 0.2 mm" (plain) · hint "or just type"
- Composer placeholder: `e.g. "I swapped the plate" or "is it connected?"`
- The wireframe note: "‹ Printers goes back to the list. Every opening is a NEW session that starts with the agent saying what it can do here; no history carried over."

### 3.3 Add flow (`#19b-add`, six states, left to right)

Entry: "+ Add printer" at the bottom of Home's printers column (`J/HomeUI/src/App.tsx`, around line 111), or "Add a printer…" in the Prepare header's printer menu (`J/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp`, around line 111), which navigates to Home first.

**A. Opener.** Pinned "NEW PRINTER", all four values `—`.
- Agent: "What printer do you have? Say it any way: "bambu a1 mini", "the ender with the touchscreen", "not sure, the small one"."
- Tip box (tinted accent background, accent left rule, camera icon): "**Tip:** a photo is the fastest way. Use **Photo** below, or drop a picture of the printer, its nameplate or the box into this panel."
- Caption "FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK", then one compact row per discovered printer:
  - a green status dot;
  - the name `Bambu Lab A1 mini` with the serial `01P00A3B` beneath it;
  - a quiet outline button **"Use this"**.
  - Omit the caption when nothing is found.
- Composer placeholder: `e.g. "bambu a1 mini" or "not sure, the small one"`

**B. Recognised from words.**
- User: "the small bambu one"
- Printer card: a picture from the profile, the name `Bambu Lab A1 mini` and the sub-line `180 × 180 × 180 mm`.
- Agent: "This one? I'll assume a **0.4 mm nozzle**, the **textured PEI plate** it ships with, and **PLA**. If anything is different, say so here or in your first project."
- Chips: **"Add this printer"** (primary, accent fill) · "Not this one"
- Pinned: Printer `Bambu Lab A1 mini` (settled) · Nozzle `0.4 mm · assumed` · Plate `Textured PEI · assumed` · Filament `PLA · assumed`
- Composer placeholder: `e.g. "I put a 0.6 nozzle on it"`

**C. Ambiguous.** Pinned values stay `—`.
- User: "the ender with the touchscreen"
- Agent: "Two Ender 3s have a touchscreen. The V2 has a knob under the screen; the S1 has none and a direct-drive extruder on the head."
- Two compact printer cards, each with a small picture, a name (`Ender-3 V2`, `Ender-3 S1`) and a quiet **"This one"** button.
- Chips: "Neither · not in the list" · hint "or a photo of the front"
  - "Neither · not in the list" opens the ConfigWizard custom-printer page, prefilled (turn 18d).
- Composer placeholder: `or say more: "it has a knob"`
- Show two or three candidates, never more (turn 18).

**D. After "Use this" on a network find.**
- A muted system line: `"Use this" · 01P00A3B`
- Printer card: the picture, `Bambu Lab A1 mini` and the sub-line `read from the printer just now`.
- Agent: "Nothing to assume: it told me its nozzle, plate and spools. To keep it connected, enter its access code (Settings › Network on the printer) or <accent link>sign in to Bambu</accent>."
- Chips: **"Add this printer"** (primary) · "Not this one"
- Pinned values are all settled, with no "assumed" suffix: `Bambu Lab A1 mini` · `0.4 mm` · `Textured PEI` · `AMS lite · ▪ PLA Matte + 3`, where ▪ is a colour swatch of the first loaded spool.
- Composer placeholder: `access code, optional`. A code typed here is saved when the printer is added; without one, the printer is added unconnected (turn 18c).
- Klipper and PrusaLink printers found by mDNS behave the same way (turn 18c), but today's discovery only lists Bambu devices (see section 4).

**E. Photo staged, not sent.** Pinned values `—`.
- Agent: "What printer do you have? Say it any way." (the short form of the opener)
- The same tip box as state A.
- The composer holds the staged-photo layout from 3.1: thumbnail `IMG_2041.jpg`, "add a note, or just send", then the Photo button, the typed text "it's this one" and the send ↑ button.

**F. Recognised from a photo.**
- User message: the sent photo (about 110×76 in the sketch) with "it's this one" under it, right-aligned.
- Printer card: the picture, `Bambu Lab A1 Combo` and the sub-line `the A1 with the AMS lite beside it`.
- Agent: "From the photo: an A1 with the four-spool AMS lite next to it, so the Combo. I'll assume a **0.4 mm nozzle** and the **textured PEI plate**; spools we'll sort out in your first project."
- Chips: **"Add this printer"** · "Not this one"
- Pinned: `Bambu Lab A1 Combo` · `0.4 mm · assumed` · `Textured PEI · assumed` · `AMS lite · 4 slots`
- Composer placeholder: `e.g. "I put a 0.6 nozzle on it"`

**After "Add this printer"** (turn 18): the printer list comes back with the new printer card on top ("as set up", or connected if an access code was given). The turn-18 "STARTER MODELS" row is not in 19b; ask Kenneth before building it.

### 3.4 No-agent state

This is decision 7, and it also covers decision 8. The panel body is the embedded agent-setup page (`AgentWebView` with `embedded=true`, which adds `?embedded=1`; see `J/AgentUI/src/main.tsx` and `App.tsx`, around line 351). The "‹ Printers" header stays. When setup completes, the panel becomes state A (Add) or the Change opener.

For the old dialog's behaviour, read `J/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupDialog.cpp` (`build_no_agent`, around line 394, and `set_up_agent`, around line 799) before deleting it. Keep its known trap: tear down the throwaway web view with `CallAfter`, not inside its own callback.

---

## 4. How the current code works

| Area | Today |
| --- | --- |
| Home page | A React app, `J/HomeUI`, shown in `J/Home/HomeWebView.cpp`. The printers column is the `<aside className="printer-column">` block in `J/HomeUI/src/App.tsx` (around lines 95–115). "+ Add printer" sends the bridge message `add_printer` → `J/Home/HomeHost.cpp` (around line 108) → `OrcaHomeBackend::add_printer` → `PrinterSetup::show_printer_setup`. Clicking a card body does nothing. The card's `…` menu (`J/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterMenu.tsx`) sends `open_printer_settings` → `OrcaHomeBackend::open_printer_settings` → `Printers::open_named_printer_settings`. |
| Old add dialog (to delete) | `J/PrinterSetup/`: `PrinterSetupDialog`, `PrinterSetupController` (states `Initial, Recognizing, Recognized, Ambiguous, Error, Complete`), `PrinterSetupLauncher`, `PrinterRecognition` (calls OpenAI directly), `PrinterPhoto`, `PrinterSetupTypes.hpp`. Keep `PrinterCatalog` and `PrinterDiscovery`; the new tools need them. |
| Agent panel | A React app, `J/AgentUI`, shown in `J/Agent/AgentWebView.cpp` and hosted by `J/Shell/AgentPane.cpp`. On Home it is deliberately collapsed (`J/Shell/ShellController.cpp`, around lines 477–525). |
| Agent host | `AgentHost`, `AgentService` and `ToolExecutionCoordinator` all take the project's `IWorkspace` (`J/Shell/ShellController.cpp`, around lines 192–204). |
| Agent instructions | A hard-coded string in `OpenAIResponsesAgent::request_body` (`J/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp`, around line 160), plus `kPrintJourneyGuidance` (`J/Agent/ToolRegistry.hpp`). The only per-request switch is `AgentRequest::Purpose` (Reply / ConversationTitle). |
| Tools | `ToolRegistry` is fixed for the life of the process. Its only per-request filter hides the import tools when no importable attachment is present. |
| Backends | Only the user's own OpenAI key works in-app. JusPrin sign-in and other providers are disabled in `Setup.tsx`. The MCP path runs the model in an external app. |
| Persistence | Every conversation goes into the project's aux dir, which is packed into the `.3mf` (`J/Agent/ProjectPersistence.hpp`). No non-persisted session exists. |
| Photos | Image attachments reach OpenAI as `input_image` (`OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp`, around line 137). |
| Tool results in the thread | Rendered only as a generic `ToolActivityCard` or a `PlanActivityCard`, and the result payload is not displayed. `SetupCard` is fed from `state.context`, not from tool results. |
| Printer helpers | `PrinterCatalog::load / find / find_device_model / models()` (no search). `discover_printers()` is a snapshot of Orca's Bambu `DeviceManager` list only. `SetupCommands::install_and_select_printer(...)`. `SetupCommands::set_printer_access_code(...)`. `Printers::add_named_printer / named_printers / rename / remove / open_named_printer_settings`. `SetupCommands::select_printer_preset / select_filament_preset / set_filament_colour / select_bed_type` change only the *current* selection. The nozzle is read-only in the printer menu because it comes from the parent system profile: each nozzle size is a separate profile variant. |
| Existing printer tools | `printer_list`, `printer_setup_preview` and `printer_setup` (`J/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, around lines 882–941) choose presets for the current job. They do not add or edit saved printers. |

---

## 5. What to build

Prompting replaces the recognition script. The five pieces below are still needed.

1. **A printer session in the agent host.** It is separate from the project conversation:
   - it has its own instructions (an Add variant and a Change variant that names the printer and its current facts);
   - it has its own tool set;
   - it never writes to project persistence, and it is discarded when the panel closes.
   - This needs a session/context parameter through `AgentHost` → `AgentService` → `OpenAIResponsesAgent::request_body`, plus per-session tool selection in place of the fixed registry list.
   - Keep the shared rules from `mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` and `architecture.md`: JavaScript renders state and sends typed commands, and C++ owns every printer change.
2. **Printer tools** (in-app exposure only, unless the MCP guide says otherwise):
   - Search the printer catalog by words: brand, model, nickname, build volume. Return the candidates with picture paths.
   - List network finds: wrap `discover_printers`.
   - Propose a printer, i.e. fill the pinned card with facts marked settled or assumed. This drives the pinned card and the printer card in the thread.
   - Add a printer: `install_and_select_printer` plus `add_named_printer`, and the access code when one is given. It runs only after the user clicks "Add this printer"; that click is the approval.
   - Read a saved printer's facts, and change its nozzle (switch to the matching profile variant), plate and spools. No helper exists for this yet. Changing a saved named printer must not silently change another project's selection.
3. **Structured thread content**:
   - the printer card (picture, name, sub-line), in full and compact variants;
   - the candidate list with "This one" buttons;
   - the "Found on your network" rows with "Use this";
   - suggestion chips (primary, suggested and plain) that send a typed action when clicked;
   - the pinned card driven by the printer session rather than `WorkspaceContext`;
   - the tip box;
   - the muted system line.
   - Extend `J/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts` additively. Per the project rule, don't bump the protocol version for additive or pre-release changes; use the capabilities list.
4. **Hosting on Home.** Show the conversation panel in place of the printers column while it is open. Reusing a second `AgentWebView` in "printer" mode (like the old dialog's embedded mode) is the likely path; confirm it against `architecture.md` before choosing. Wire up:
   - "‹ Printers" to close the panel;
   - "Set it up myself" (decision 5);
   - the drop zone;
   - Prepare-header "Add a printer…" and "Printer settings…" to navigate to Home and open the panel (decision 4).
5. **Deletions.** Remove:
   - `J/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupDialog.*`, `PrinterSetupController.*`, `PrinterSetupLauncher.*` (keep `run_manual_setup`'s ConfigWizard behaviour somewhere), `PrinterRecognition.*`, `PrinterPhoto.*`, and any type in `PrinterSetupTypes.hpp` that nothing uses any more;
   - the `printerSetup` dialog tokens, if unused (`J/Shell/ShellTheme.cpp`, around line 204), with their guards in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` and `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp`;
   - `tests/jusprin/test_printer_setup.cpp`;
   - `tests/shell/fake_printer_recognition.cpp`;
   - the harness's `verify_printer_setup` path (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`), which you replace with a panel check;
   - the CMake entries for all of these.

Before touching any OrcaSlicer-owned file (anything outside `J/`), read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.

---

## 6. Open questions to raise with Kenneth (the wireframes don't cover them)

- What "‹ Printers" does in the middle of an Add conversation: discard silently, or confirm?
- The error states: agent request failed, no match at all, network printer went offline between "Use this" and Add, access code rejected. Turn 18 says one error at a time, each with its fix.
- Whether "Not this one" re-asks with the other candidates or returns to the opener.
- Whether the Change session can also connect a printer (the Change opener mentions "connection").
- Whether to build the post-Add STARTER MODELS row (turn 18).

---

## 7. Verification expected

- **Vitest** for the new AgentUI and HomeUI components and for the protocol additions. Prove each guard test fails first by injecting the violation.
- **Catch2** for the printer tools and the session separation: a printer session writes nothing to project persistence.
- **Shell harness** (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, isolated `--datadir` and `$HOME`), extended to:
  - open the panel from "+ Add printer";
  - add a printer through the fake Bambu device (`J/Testing/README.md`);
  - open the panel from "Printer settings…".
- **Visual check**: render every state in 3.2–3.4 in the running app, or render the widgets to a bitmap, and compare each against the matching wireframe panel for structure, order, copy and emphasis. Check light and dark themes, and Windows as well as macOS (Windows text renders about 9% larger).

I wrote the handoff document to [agent-docs/jusprin/printer-conversation-panel-handoff.md](agent-docs/jusprin/printer-conversation-panel-handoff.md). It's in the working tree but not committed. It has everything an implementing agent needs: where the design lives, what you decided, every panel state, and what to build and delete.

**What's in it:**
- **Design sources:** the design project ID and exactly what to read in it: the 19b (Change) and 19b-add (Add) panels, the turn-18 screens it inherits from, and the relevant sections of the design's decision log. It also says how to view the wireframes locally, since they only render when served over HTTP.
- **What "pixel-perfect" means here:** the wireframes are rough sketches (sketch font, beige palette, a 250 px column in a 660 px drawing). The document tells the agent to match structure, element order, emphasis and wording exactly, and to take every colour, size and font from the existing design-token file. It maps each wireframe element to the app component whose look to reuse. The panel width is Home's existing printers-column width, 320 px.
- **Your decisions:**
  - Home's printers column becomes the chat panel.
  - The real agent handles adding and changing printers.
  - "Printer settings…" opens the panel, both on Home and in the Prepare screen's header.
  - "Set it up myself" opens the setup wizard when adding, and OrcaSlicer's settings window when changing a printer.
  - The old dialog is deleted.
  - With no agent, or with an external AI app connected, the panel shows the agent setup page.
- **Every panel state, with exact wording:** the change chat and the six add states (opening message, recognised from words, several matches, after "Use this", photo staged, recognised from a photo), plus the no-agent state. Each lists the pinned-card values and their styles, the suggestion buttons and the text-box placeholder.
- **Where today's code lives** (file references), and **the build list**: the separate Home chat session, the new printer tools, the chat cards, placing the panel on Home, and the files and tests to delete.
- **Verification expected:** unit tests, the test harness, and a visual comparison against each wireframe state in light and dark themes, on macOS and Windows.

**Changes from the wireframes:**
- **Re-slice sentence removed.** In the change example, the agent's reply no longer says your projects will re-slice with the new nozzle, because nothing in the app does that yet.
- **Starter-models row not included.** The turn-18 row of suggested models after adding a printer isn't in 19b, so the document tells the agent to ask you before building it.

**Questions the agent will bring to you, since the wireframes don't answer them:**
- Does "‹ Printers" in the middle of adding a printer discard the conversation silently or ask first?
- What do the error states look like (agent failure, no match, printer went offline, wrong access code)?
- Does "Not this one" offer the other candidates or start over?
- Can the change chat also connect a printer?

---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed

content.text:
The agent is checking what a nozzle change should affect. In the app, a saved printer like "My A1 Combo" is a single shared record, and projects refer to it by name rather than keeping their own copy. So if you tell the chat "I put a 0.6 nozzle on it", the agent is asking whether every project that uses that printer should now slice for 0.6, while projects set up for a different printer stay unchanged.

In code terms, a saved printer is an OrcaSlicer user printer profile that inherits from a shipped profile ([NamedPrinters.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.hpp)). OrcaSlicer ships a separate profile for each nozzle size, e.g. "Bambu Lab A1 0.4 nozzle" and "Bambu Lab A1 0.6 nozzle". So the nozzle change has to point your saved printer at the 0.6 profile, and that saved printer is shared by every project that uses it.

**My recommendation: answer yes.** The nozzle is a physical fact about the machine, and the design treats printer facts as belonging to the printer, not the project. The wireframe even had the agent say your projects on that printer would re-slice with the new nozzle. You asked me to drop that sentence only because nothing implements the re-slicing yet, not because the idea was wrong.

**One thing to have the agent check first.** A saved project file also keeps its own copy of the printer settings from the last time it was saved. I haven't checked what OrcaSlicer does when you reopen such a project after the saved printer changed: use the updated printer, use the project's old copy, or ask you. That decides whether "every project follows the change" actually happens.

A reply you could send:

> Yes. The nozzle is a fact about the physical machine, so every project using that saved printer should follow it; projects on other printers are untouched. Before building, check what happens when an existing project file that still holds the old nozzle settings is reopened, and tell me.

(b) Change only the nozzle and the connection, and just show plate and spools for information.

content.text:
The agent is asking how much the change chat is allowed to actually save, versus just display. The pinned card at the top of the panel always shows four rows — Printer, Nozzle, Plate, Filament — so if you say "I swapped to the smooth plate" or "this reel is done", the agent needs to know whether it can record that on the printer or only talk about it.

- **(a)** means a saved printer gains its own default plate, and its spools can be edited from the chat.
- **(b)** means only the nozzle and the network connection can be changed. Plate and spools appear on the card as facts to look at, and changing them still happens in the project, as it does today.

The agent's reason for preferring (b) is that OrcaSlicer has no "default plate" on a printer. The plate type is stored per project, so adding one to a printer means adding a field to OrcaSlicer's own printer profiles — the kind of change to upstream code this fork tries to avoid.

**That reasoning holds for the plate, but not for spools.** This fork already has its own storage for spools, kept per printer, outside the project file and outside OrcaSlicer's profiles: `SpoolStore` in [SpoolStore.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SpoolStore.hpp), described there as "Remembered spools, a fork-owned concept OrcaSlicer does not have… remembered per printer." Editing spools from the change chat writes to that store and touches no OrcaSlicer profile. So (b) gives up something you already have.

The same trick could give the printer a default plate without touching OrcaSlicer: keep it in a small fork-owned store, the way spools are kept, and apply it when a project uses that printer. That's more work than (b), and it's a product decision about whether the plate is a fact about the machine or a choice per project.

**My recommendation, split three ways:**
- **Nozzle and connection: editable**, as the agent proposed.
- **Spools: editable** through the existing spool store, not read-only.
- **Plate: read-only for now**, changed in the project as it is today. Revisit it later if you want a default plate per printer.

A reply you could send:

> Nozzle and connection: editable, agreed. Spools: also editable — use the existing fork-owned SpoolStore (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SpoolStore.hpp), which already remembers spools per printer outside Orca's profiles, so no upstream setting is needed. Plate: read-only for now, still changed per project; a per-printer default plate would need a fork-owned store too, and that's a product decision I'll make separately.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-09T16:51:11.156Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

metadata:

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

input.content:
# Printer conversation panel — hands-on test report

Build tested: worktree `printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`, commit "Talk to the agent about a printer, where the printers column is" (0e55c4f9be), macOS, RelWithDebInfo.
How: the built binary was launched against a throwaway copy of the JusPrin data directory and an isolated `$HOME`, and driven by real clicks and typing. The agent was the real OpenAI-backed in-app agent. A second run used the same data directory with the agent's API key removed.

## What works

- The printers column is replaced by the conversation panel, the projects gallery stays visible, and "‹ Printers" returns to the list.
- The opening message, the photo tip and the empty pinned card match the wireframe.
- Recognition from words works ("the small bambu one" → Bambu Lab A1 mini card with assumptions).
- Recognition from a photo works (a picture of an A1 mini was identified).
- "Add this printer" saves the printer and returns to the list.
- The change conversation opens from a printer card's "Printer settings…", the nozzle change goes through an approval card, and the pinned card shows "0.6 mm · changed" in red.
- The nozzle change is real and persists: the saved printer profile now inherits `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.6 nozzle`.

## Not covered

Network "Use this" (no printers on this network), dropping a photo onto the panel, dark theme, Windows.

## Findings by severity

### High

**H1. With no agent set up there is no way forward and no way to set one up.**
The panel opens the normal add conversation: the agent's opener, the photo tip, and a composer whose placeholder reads "The Agent is not available". The Photo button does nothing. There is no setup card and no link. The agreed behaviour was the embedded agent-setup page the old dialog used.

**H2. Loose wording never produces candidate cards; the conversation dead-ends.**
"the ender with the touchscreen" → "I couldn't find a match from that alone." "not sure, either the v2 or the s1" → "I can't tell which one from that." "maybe ender 3 v2 or ender 3 s1" → "I couldn't find a packaged match for that wording." Only the exact "ender 3 v2" produced a card. The two picture cards, "Neither · not in the list" and the escape to the wizard never appear, and the agent never mentions "Set it up myself".
Cause (verified in code): `OrcaPrinterBackend::search_catalog` requires **every** word of the query to appear in "vendor + model + build volume + model id", while the session instructions tell the model to search with "the person's own words". Any conversational phrasing therefore returns nothing.

**H3. "Printer settings…" in the Prepare header opens the ADD conversation.**
From a project with "Generic Klipper Printer" selected, the menu item navigates to Home and opens "NEW PRINTER / What printer do you have?" instead of a conversation about that printer. Likely because the selected printer is a system preset rather than a saved named printer, but the person is simply given the wrong screen with no explanation.

**H4. A sent photo stays staged in the composer.**
After sending, the thumbnail and "add a note, or just send" remain, so the next message would carry the same photo again. Reproduced twice.

**H5. An assistant message was rendered twice, concatenated.**
"Okay—tell me the brand, model, or what the printer looks like, and I'll match it.Okay—tell me the brand, model, or what the printer looks like, and I'll match it."

**H6. "Not this one" leaves the rejected printer in place.**
The pinned card keeps the rejected model and its assumptions, and the "Add this printer" chip stays enabled, so the printer that was just rejected can still be added.

### Medium

**M1. The vendor name is duplicated in every printer name.**
"Bambulab Bambu Lab A1 mini", "Creality Creality Ender-3 V2". It is also saved as the printer's name and then truncated on the Home card ("Bambulab Bambu Lab …").

**M2. The approval card does not say what will change.**
It reads "Change this printer / printer_change · jusprin-native / Waiting for your approval". It never says 0.4 mm → 0.6 mm, and it shows the internal tool id to the user.

**M3. Empty agent bubbles.**
One or two avatar dots with no text appear before each reply while tools run.

**M4. The chips are docked at the bottom, far from the message they answer.**
With a short thread there is a large empty gap between the card and the chips; the agent even said "Tap the card if you want to add it", but the card is not tappable. The wireframe puts the chips directly under the message, with the composer beneath them.

**M5. The pinned card shows preset jargon and loses the "assumed" marks.**
In the add flow it read "Textured PEI Plate" and "Bambu PLA Matte @BBL A1M" with no "· assumed" suffix; the wireframe wants "0.4 mm · assumed", "Textured PEI · assumed", "PLA · assumed".

**M6. "Set it up myself" discards the conversation and starts from scratch.**
The stock wizard opens as a floating dialog over Home while the panel stays behind it, nothing the agent inferred is pre-selected, and cancelling the wizard closes the panel and loses the thread with no way back.

**M7. After adding, the new printer is appended at the bottom of the list, with no confirmation.**
The wireframe puts the new card on top.

### Low

**L1.** The composer placeholder is clipped: `e.g. "bambu a1 mini" or "not sure, the small` — the rest is cut off.
**L2.** A staged photo sits above the composer box as a wide file row; the wireframe puts a square thumbnail inside the box, above the text line.
**L3.** A sent photo appears in the thread as a file-name chip, not as the picture.
**L4.** No follow-up chips after the nozzle change; the wireframe offers "Use 0.3 mm layers" / "Keep 0.2 mm".
