content.text:
I ran the built app from that worktree against a throwaway copy of your data directory, drove it by real clicks and typing with the live agent, and then ran it a second time with the agent's API key removed. The core flows work: the printers column becomes a chat panel, the agent recognises a printer from words and from a photo, adding saves it, and the nozzle change is real — the saved printer profile now inherits "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.6 nozzle". Six problems are serious enough to fix before this ships.

I didn't test network discovery (nothing on this network), dragging a photo onto the panel, dark theme, or Windows.

## High

**1. With no agent set up, the panel is a dead end.** It opens the normal add conversation — agent greeting, photo tip — but the text box is disabled and reads "The Agent is not available", and the Photo button does nothing. There is no setup card and no link to set one up. You decided this state should show the same agent-setup page the old dialog embedded.

**2. Loose wording never produces the two picture cards; the conversation goes in circles.** "the ender with the touchscreen" → "I couldn't find a match from that alone." "not sure, either the v2 or the s1" → "I can't tell which one from that." "maybe ender 3 v2 or ender 3 s1" → "I couldn't find a packaged match for that wording." Only the exact words "ender 3 v2" produced a card. The user is never offered candidates, "Neither · not in the list", or the manual wizard.
The cause is in the code: the catalog search requires **every** word of the query to appear in the printer's vendor, model, build volume or id ([OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:103](.claude/worktrees/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:103)), while the agent's instructions tell it to search with "the person's own words" ([PrinterConversation.cpp:191](.claude/worktrees/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:191)). Any conversational phrase returns nothing.

**3. "Printer settings…" in the Prepare screen's header opens the ADD conversation.** With "Generic Klipper Printer" selected, it went to Home and showed "NEW PRINTER / What printer do you have?" instead of a conversation about that printer. My guess is that the selected printer is a shipped profile rather than a saved printer, but either way the user gets the wrong screen with no explanation.

**4. A sent photo stays staged in the text box.** After sending, the thumbnail and "add a note, or just send" are still there, so the next message would send the same photo again. Reproduced twice.

**5. One agent reply was rendered twice, run together:** "Okay—tell me the brand, model, or what the printer looks like, and I'll match it.Okay—tell me the brand, model, or what the printer looks like, and I'll match it."

**6. "Not this one" leaves the rejected printer in place.** The pinned card keeps it and "Add this printer" stays enabled, so you can still add the printer you just rejected.

## Medium

**7. The brand name is doubled in every printer name:** "Bambulab Bambu Lab A1 mini", "Creality Creality Ender-3 V2". It's also saved as the printer's name and then truncated on the Home card as "Bambulab Bambu Lab …".

**8. The approval card doesn't say what will change.** It reads "Change this printer / printer_change · jusprin-native / Waiting for your approval". It never says 0.4 mm → 0.6 mm, and it shows an internal tool name to the user.

**9. Empty agent bubbles.** One or two avatar dots with no text appear before each reply while the agent is running its tools.

**10. The action buttons are docked at the bottom, far from the message they answer.** With a short conversation there's a large blank gap between the printer card and the buttons. The agent even said "Tap the card if you want to add it", but the card isn't clickable. The wireframe puts the buttons directly under the message.

**11. The pinned card shows internal preset names and drops the "assumed" marks:** "Textured PEI Plate" and "Bambu PLA Matte @BBL A1M", instead of "Textured PEI · assumed" and "PLA · assumed".

**12. "Set it up myself" throws the conversation away.** The stock wizard opens as a floating dialog over Home with the panel still behind it, nothing the agent inferred is pre-selected, and cancelling it closes the panel and loses the thread with no way back.

**13. A newly added printer goes to the bottom of the list, with no confirmation.** The wireframe puts the new card on top.

## Low

**14.** The text box placeholder is cut off: `e.g. "bambu a1 mini" or "not sure, the small`.

# Add a printer — first-time-user test report

Same build (worktree `printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`, commit 0e55c4f9be), fresh copy of the data directory, live OpenAI-backed agent. This run typed what a person who has never seen the flow would type.

The headline: the flow only works if you type the printer's catalog name almost exactly. Ordinary phrasing gets a confident "not found" for printers that are in the catalog, or a confident match to the wrong printer, and there is no list to browse and no way out.

## Critical

**C1. Correct model names are rejected over a space. "voron 2.4 350mm" → "I couldn't find a packaged profile that matches a Voron 2.4 350mm." "voron 2.4 350" → found instantly.**
The catalog contains `Voron 2.4 350`. Search requires every word of the query to appear as a substring of "vendor + model + build volume + model id" ([OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:103](.claude/worktrees/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:103)); "350mm" is not a substring of "... 350 350 x 350 x 325 mm". The user is told their printer is unsupported. No fuzzy matching, no partial-match fallback, no "did you mean".

**C2. A common nickname matched a different manufacturer's printer, stated as certain.** "x1c" → "Orca Arena Printer Orca Arena X1 Carbon", with "I found one clear match". Bambu Lab's X1 Carbon is in the catalog; it does not contain the literal string "x1c", while the Orca Arena profile's internal model id does. A first-time user adds a wrong profile — wrong bed size, wrong G-code flavour — and has no way to know.

**C3. Truncated search results are presented as the complete list.** "prusa" → three cards (CORE One, CORE One HF, CORE One L) and "I found three Prusa matches that fit 'prusa'". Prusa ships 13 models in the catalog; MK4, MK3S and MINI were never shown. The search returns the first N in file order and the result carries no total and no "truncated" flag, so the agent states a falsehood with confidence. A MK3S owner is shown three printers that are not theirs.

**C4. A printer that genuinely is not in the catalog has no exit.** "i built it myself, a voron 2.4 350mm" → "tell me the exact controller or kit name". "it runs klipper on a btt octopus board" → "give me the exact Voron variant name". The agent never offers the manual wizard, never mentions "Generic Klipper Printer" (which exists in the catalog), and never points at the "Set it up myself" link. The conversation loops until the user gives up.

**C5. There is no way to browse.** "can you show me a list of the brands you support so i can pick" → "I can't show a brand list from here." The old dialog had the vendor/model grid; here the only access to it is a small "Set it up myself" link in the panel header, which the agent never mentions and which a newcomer will read as "do it the hard way". A person who does not know their model's exact name is stuck.

**C6. The agent promises to do things it cannot do, and wanders off-product.** "how do i connect it to my computer?" → advice about USB and PrusaLink/PrusaConnect plus "I can help you with the simplest setup". Follow-up "yes please, set it up so i can print to it" → "I can't set it up directly from here... tell me Windows, Mac, or Linux and I'll give you the exact next steps" (the app knows it is on a Mac). There is no connection tool and no Connect… entry point in this build, so this is a dead end dressed as help.

## High

**H1. Nothing tells the user what this flow does or where it ends.** The opener asks for a printer name. It never says that this adds a printer profile, that nothing is being connected, that nozzle/plate/filament will be assumed and can be corrected later, or what happens after "Add this printer". A first-time user cannot tell whether they are configuring a machine, connecting to it, or starting a print.

**H2. After adding, the user is dropped back to the list with no confirmation and no next step.** No "added", no starter models, no hint about connecting or opening a project. The card's status dot is unexplained: a newcomer cannot tell whether the printer is connected.

**H3. Going back loses the whole conversation, silently.** "‹ Printers" during a conversation discards it with no warning, and reopening starts a new session. Cancelling the wizard reached through "Set it up myself" does the same. A person who steps back to check the printer list loses everything they typed.

**H4. The agent tells the user to tap things that are not tappable.** "Tap the card to add it", "Tap 'Add this printer' on the card" — the card is inert and the button is docked at the bottom of the panel, far from the card. When several cards have accumulated in one conversation, it is not clear which one the bottom button applies to (it is always the newest).

**H5. Rejected and superseded printers stay on screen.** After "no it's the bambu one", the wrong Orca Arena card is still in the thread above the right one, and both look equally live. After "Not this one", the pinned card still holds the rejected printer and "Add this printer" stays enabled.

**H6. Every printer's name is doubled, and that name is what gets saved.** "Prusa Prusa MK3S", "Bambulab Bambu Lab X1 Carbon", "Orca Arena Printer Orca Arena X1 Carbon". The saved printer is then truncated in the Home list ("Bambulab Bambu Lab …"). A newcomer reads this as the app being broken.

**H7. Adding a printer marks the open project as modified.** The window title changed from "Untitled" to "*Untitled" right after "Add this printer", so the user is later asked to save a project they never touched. (Observed once, immediately after adding; not isolated further.)

## Medium

**M1. The pinned card is unexplained jargon.** "NEW PRINTER / Printer — / Nozzle — / Plate — / Filament —" appears before the user has typed anything, with four em dashes. Nothing says it will fill in as the conversation goes, or that "assumed" means "we guessed, fix it later". In the add flow the "· assumed" marks were missing entirely; Plate was left blank for the Prusa.

**M2. The example answers are the only instruction, and they are clipped.** The text box placeholder reads `e.g. "bambu a1 mini" or "not sure, the small` — the rest is cut off. Given C1–C3, the examples also teach the wrong lesson: "not sure, the small one" is exactly the phrasing that fails.

**M3. Search quality is invisible to the user.** No result count, no "showing 3 of 13", no way to ask for more. The user cannot tell a real absence from a truncated list.

**M4. Empty agent bubbles while tools run.** One to three avatar dots with no text appear before each reply. A newcomer reads them as messages that failed to load.

**M5. A sent photo appears as a file-name chip, not the picture,** and the staged photo stays in the box after sending, so the next message re-sends it.

**M6. "Set it up myself" is unexplained.** It sits in the panel header on every screen with no hint that it opens the standard printer wizard, and it is the only route to the brand list.

## What a first-time user should have been given

1. An opener that states the job and its end: "I'll add your printer so projects can slice for it. This doesn't connect to it yet."
2. A way to browse when they cannot name their printer: brand chips, or a plain "show me a list" that opens the wizard grid inside the panel.
3. Search that tolerates ordinary phrasing: partial matches, model-number normalisation ("350mm" = "350"), nicknames ("x1c", "mk3"), and a vendor preference so a community profile never outranks the manufacturer's.
4. Honest results: how many matched, which are shown, and an offer to narrow down — never "I found three matches" when there are thirteen.
5. One always-present escape: "I can't find it" → the wizard, prefilled with whatever was understood.
6. After adding: a line confirming what was added and what to do next, with the new printer at the top of the list.

17. **Adding a printer marks the open project as modified** ("Untitled" → "*Untitled"), so the user is later asked to save a project they never touched. Observed once.
18. **The agent says "tap the card", but cards are inert** and the real button is docked at the bottom of the panel, far from the card it belongs to.

19. **The pinned card is unexplained jargon,** shown with four em dashes before anything is typed; the "· assumed" marks were missing in the add flow and Plate stayed blank for the Prusa.

# Printer conversation panel — findings

What is wrong, and the evidence for it. No recommendations: how to fix each one is the implementer's call.

Build: worktree `printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`, commit 0e55c4f9be ("Talk to the agent about a printer, where the printers column is"), macOS, RelWithDebInfo.
Method: the built binary was run against throwaway copies of the JusPrin data directory with an isolated `$HOME`, driven by real clicks and typing, with the live OpenAI-backed in-app agent. Three runs: a walk through both flows, a run with the agent's API key removed, and a run typing what a person who has never seen the flow would type. Paths are relative to that worktree.

Severity: **Critical** — the user is blocked, or ends up with the wrong printer without knowing. **High** — the flow completes but misleads, loses work, or an agreed part of the design is absent. **Medium** — confusing but recoverable. **Low** — polish.

Not covered: network "Use this" (nothing on this network), dragging a photo onto the panel, dark theme, Windows.

## What works

The printers column is replaced by the panel and "‹ Printers" returns to the list. Recognition from an exact model name works, and from a photo of a printer. "Add this printer" saves the printer. The change conversation opens from a printer card, the nozzle change goes through an approval card, the pinned card shows "0.6 mm · changed", and the change is real and persists: the saved profile now inherits `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.6 nozzle`. Replies stream, so there is feedback while the agent is writing.

## Critical

**1. Ordinary phrasing produces a false "not found" for printers that are in the catalog.**
"i built it myself, a voron 2.4 350mm" → "I couldn't find a packaged profile that matches a Voron 2.4 350mm." "voron 2.4 350" → found immediately. The catalog contains `Voron 2.4 350`. Same failure for "the ender with the touchscreen", "not sure, either the v2 or the s1", and "maybe ender 3 v2 or ender 3 s1", while "ender 3 v2" matched.
Mechanism: `OrcaPrinterBackend::search_catalog` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:103) keeps a model only when **every** word of the query is a substring of "vendor + model + build volume + model id"; the session instructions (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:191) tell the agent to search with "the person's own words". "350mm" is not a substring of "350 × 350 × 325 mm".

**2. A common nickname matched another manufacturer's printer, and the agent stated it as certain.**
"x1c" → card "Orca Arena Printer Orca Arena X1 Carbon" with "I found one clear match and assumed a 0.4 mm nozzle with PLA." Both `Bambu Lab X1 Carbon` (BBL) and `Orca Arena X1 Carbon` (OrcaArena) are in the catalog; the Bambu entry's text does not contain the literal "x1c". Correcting it with "no it's the bambu one" worked, but only because the tester knew.

**3. Truncated search results are presented as the complete set.**
"prusa" → three cards (CORE One, CORE One HF, CORE One L) and "I found three Prusa matches that fit 'prusa'". The catalog ships 13 Prusa models; MK4, MK3S and MINI were not among them. "prusa mk3s" then matched MK3S. The search returns the first N in catalog order and the result carries no total and no truncation flag.

**4. With no agent set up the panel is a dead end.**
It opens the normal add conversation — greeting, photo tip — with the text box disabled and reading "The Agent is not available", and the Photo button inert. No setup card, no link, no explanation. The agreed behaviour was the embedded agent-setup page the old dialog used. Verified with a data directory whose `jusprin_agent` entry was removed.

**5. A printer that genuinely is not in the catalog has no exit.**
"i built it myself, a voron 2.4 350mm" → "tell me the exact controller or kit name"; "it runs klipper on a btt octopus board" → "give me the exact Voron variant name". The manual wizard is never offered, the shipped `Generic Klipper Printer` profile is never mentioned, and the header's "Set it up myself" link is never referred to.

**6. There is no way to browse what the app supports.**
"actually can you show me a list of the brands you support so i can pick" → "I can't show a brand list from here." The brand and model grid exists only behind the header link.

## High

**7. The agent offers help it cannot deliver, and leaves the product.**
"how do i connect it to my computer?" → USB and PrusaLink/PrusaConnect advice plus "I can help you with the simplest setup". "yes please, set it up so i can print to it" → "I can't set it up directly from here… If you tell me Windows, Mac, or Linux, I'll give you the exact next steps", while running on the user's Mac. There is no connection tool in the session and no Connect… entry point in this build.

**8. "Printer settings…" in the Prepare header opens the ADD conversation.**
From a project with "Generic Klipper Printer" selected, the menu item navigated to Home and showed "NEW PRINTER / What printer do you have?" instead of a conversation about that printer. That printer is a shipped profile rather than a saved printer.

**9. Nothing states what the flow does or where it ends.**
The opener asks for a printer name. It never says that this adds a printer profile, that nothing is being connected, that nozzle, plate and filament will be assumed and corrected later, or what happens after "Add this printer".

**10. Leaving the conversation destroys it silently.**
"‹ Printers" mid-conversation discards the thread with no warning; reopening starts a new session. Cancelling the wizard reached through "Set it up myself" closes the panel and loses the thread the same way.

**11. Every printer's name is doubled, and the doubled name is saved.**
"Prusa Prusa MK3S", "Bambulab Bambu Lab X1 Carbon", "Creality Creality Ender-3 V2", "Orca Arena Printer Orca Arena X1 Carbon". The saved printer appears truncated in the Home list ("Bambulab Bambu Lab …").

**12. Rejected and superseded printers stay live.**
After "Not this one", the pinned card still holds the rejected printer and "Add this printer" is still enabled. After a correction, the wrong card remains in the thread above the right one, looking equally current.

**13. A sent photo stays staged in the composer.**
After sending, the thumbnail and "add a note, or just send" remain, so the next message would carry the same photo again. Reproduced twice.

**14. An assistant message was rendered twice, concatenated.**
"Okay—tell me the brand, model, or what the printer looks like, and I'll match it.Okay—tell me the brand, model, or what the printer looks like, and I'll match it."

**15. The approval card does not say what will change.**
It reads "Change this printer / printer_change · jusprin-native / Waiting for your approval". It never says 0.4 mm → 0.6 mm, and it shows the internal tool name to the user.

**16. After adding: no confirmation, no next step, and the new printer is appended at the bottom of the list.**
The card's status dot is unexplained, so it is not apparent whether the printer is connected.

**17. Adding a printer marks the open project as modified.**
The window title changed from "Untitled" to "*Untitled" immediately after "Add this printer", so a save prompt appears later for a project the user never edited. Observed once; not isolated further.

**18. The agent tells the user to tap things that are not tappable.**
"Tap the card to add it", "Tap 'Add this printer' on the card". The cards are inert; the button is docked at the bottom of the panel, separated from the card by empty space, and when several cards have accumulated nothing indicates which one it applies to (it is the newest).

## Medium

**19. The pinned card is unexplained.**
"NEW PRINTER / Printer — / Nozzle — / Plate — / Filament —" is shown before anything is typed. In the add flow the "· assumed" suffixes were missing, values were preset jargon ("Textured PEI Plate", "Bambu PLA Matte @BBL A1M"), and Plate stayed blank for the Prusa.

**20. The composer placeholder is clipped and demonstrates phrasing that fails.**
It renders as `e.g. "bambu a1 mini" or "not sure, the small` with the rest cut off, and "not sure, the small one" is the kind of phrasing finding 1 breaks on.

**21. Search quality is invisible.** No result count, no "showing 3 of 13", no way to ask for more, so an absence cannot be told from a truncation.

**22. Empty agent bubbles.** One to three avatar dots with no text appear before each reply while tools run.

**23. "Set it up myself" is unexplained and disruptive.** No hint that it opens the standard printer wizard; the wizard opens as a floating dialog over Home with the panel still behind it, and nothing the agent inferred is pre-selected.

**24. Photos.** A staged photo sits above the composer box as a wide file row rather than a thumbnail inside it, and a sent photo appears in the thread as a file name rather than the picture.

## Low

**25. No follow-up suggestions after a change.** The nozzle change produced no chips; the wireframe offers "Use 0.3 mm layers" / "Keep 0.2 mm".

The merged file now exists and contains problems only: 25 findings, ranked critical to low, each with what was typed and what appeared. I kept two kinds of non-problem material, and you should tell me if you want either removed:

- **Root causes I verified in the code** — for example that the catalog search keeps a model only when every word of the query is a substring of its text. That's an observation, and without it the search findings read as random flakiness.
- **A short "what works" paragraph** at the top, so the implementer knows which parts not to rewrite.

Removed: the six "what a first-time user should have been given" recommendations and the suggested fix order. Say the word and I'll put them back as a separate document, so the findings stay clean either way.
propose a better ux/ui design for each of these problems.  Be honest with yourself and if you don't have idea for a better ux/ui, just say so

Here are concrete proposals. Three design moves cover ten of the findings, so I'll describe those first, then the rest one by one, then the ones where I have no design to offer.

## Three moves that cover ten findings

**Move A — the app renders search results, not the agent's prose.** (covers 2, 3, 21, and the visible half of 1)

When the agent searches, the panel draws a results block it controls:

```
MATCHES FOR "prusa"          3 of 13  ▸ Show all
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ [pic]  PRUSA                     │
│        MK3S              This one│
│        250 × 210 × 210 mm        │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

- The brand is its own small line above the model, so "Prusa Prusa MK3S" can't happen (also fixes 11).
- The count and "Show all" come from the search result, not the model's summary, so "I found three matches" can never contradict a catalog of thirteen.
- A profile that isn't from the manufacturer is labelled on the card: `COMMUNITY PROFILE · Orca Arena`. When two vendors have the same model name, both cards are always shown and the manufacturer's is first — no single "clear match" (fixes 2).

**Move B — a browsable list inside the panel.** (covers 5, 6, 23, and gives 1 a floor)

A "Browse all printers" chip in the opener, and the header link renamed from "Set it up myself" to "Browse the full list". Both open a picker *inside* the panel, not a floating dialog: a filter box, then brands as rows, then models as rows with thumbnails, with "‹" back at each level. Its last row is "My printer isn't listed" → the custom-printer wizard, pre-filled with anything the conversation already established.

This gives the flow a floor: however badly the search behaves, there is always a visible way to find your printer by eye. It also means the no-match state has somewhere to point (fixes 5): the panel appends a standing row above the composer after any failed search — `Not finding it? Browse the full list · Set it up manually`.

**Move C — the card owns its action; dead cards look dead.** (covers 12, 18)

Every proposed printer carries its own button, in the single-match case too ("Add this one" / "This one"). The docked bar at the bottom keeps only conversation-level replies. When a card is superseded or rejected, it collapses to one grey line — `Not this one · Orca Arena X1 Carbon` — and loses its button, so only one live card exists at a time. If you keep a docked button as well, it must name its target: "Add Bambu Lab X1 Carbon", never a bare "Add this printer".

## The rest, one at a time

**1 — search rejects ordinary phrasing.** The matching itself is engineering, not UI: score matches instead of requiring every word, drop filler words ("the", "my", "maybe", "not sure"), normalise "350mm" to "350" and "mk3"/"MK3S", and match on prefixes. The UI contribution is Move A's count and Move B's floor. I have no clever interface that rescues a bad matcher.

**4 — no agent set up.** Replace the fake conversation with the setup screen, but keep the parts that don't need an agent: header stays, pinned card hidden, body is `Set up the agent — it identifies your printer from a name or a photo` with the primary setup button; below it, still live, any printers found on the network with "Use this", plus "Browse the full list". So the panel is useful without an agent instead of being a disabled text box.

**7 — the agent promises to connect the printer.** Add a fifth pinned row, `Connection — not set up`, so the subject is on screen and owned by the UI rather than the chat. The agent's line becomes one product-true sentence plus a chip that goes where connecting actually happens. **Honest caveat:** I could not find a Connect… entry point in this build, so the chip has nowhere to go yet. Until that exists, this is a product gap, and the only honest design is the agent saying "I can't connect printers yet."

**8 — "Printer settings…" in Prepare opens the Add flow.** It should open the change conversation for the printer that's actually selected. When that printer is a shipped profile rather than one of your saved printers, open the change panel anyway with the pinned card filled from the profile and one line — `This printer isn't in your list yet` — and a chip `Add it to my printers`. That turns today's wrong screen into the natural next step.

**9 — nothing explains the flow.** The opener becomes two lines: what this does and where it stops — `I'll set up your printer so projects slice for it. This doesn't connect to it; that comes after.` — then the examples. Under the pinned card, one caption: `I'll fill this in as we go. Anything marked "assumed" you can change later.`

**10 — going back destroys the conversation.** Keep the draft session alive while the app runs: "‹ Printers" returns to the list, and reopening "+ Add printer" restores what you typed, with a `Start over` action in the header. Every add still begins fresh after a printer is added or after "Start over". **This is your call, not mine** — it softens your "every opening is a new session" rule. The cheaper alternative is a confirm on exit once the thread has content, which I like less because it punishes curiosity with a dialog.

**11 — doubled names.** Display brand and model as separate fields (Move A). Save the model name alone as the printer's name, adding "2" when you already own that model. Optionally let the name be edited on the confirmation strip in 16 — people name their machines.

**13 — sent photo stays staged.** Clear the staged attachment on send and show the picture in the thread. No design question; it's a bug.

**14 — message rendered twice.** Bug, no design.

**15 — approval card says nothing.** Rewrite it as the sentence it stands for:

```
Change nozzle
0.4 mm → 0.6 mm on Bambu Lab A1 mini
Every project that uses this printer slices for 0.6 mm.
                              [Approve]  Reject
```

The tool name belongs behind a small "details" disclosure, or nowhere.

**16 — nothing after adding.** Don't just close. Return to the list with the new card at the top, briefly highlighted, and one dismissible strip above it: `Bambu Lab A1 mini added · 0.4 mm nozzle, Textured PEI, PLA · Not connected`, with `Connect` and `Change` links. That answers "did it work", "what did it assume", and "what now" in one line.

**17 — adding a printer dirties the open project.** I have no UI design for this; the project must simply not be marked modified. Engineering fix.

**19 — the pinned card is unexplained jargon.** Human values, not preset ids: `Plate — Textured PEI (assumed)`, `Filament — PLA (assumed)`, mapping "Bambu PLA Matte @BBL A1M" to "PLA Matte". Before anything is known, keep the four rows greyed under the caption from 9 rather than four bare em dashes.

**20 — clipped placeholder.** One line that truncates with an ellipsis, and shorter: `e.g. "bambu a1 mini"`. The richer examples live in the opener, which has room. The box grows to two lines only when the person types.

**22 — empty agent bubbles.** No bubble until there is text. While tools run, one inline status line that names the work — `Searching the printer list…` — which collapses when the reply arrives.

**24 — photos.** Thumbnail inside the composer box above the text line, with its × on the corner; in the thread, the picture itself at about 120 px wide with any note beneath it.

**25 — no follow-up after a change.** After an applied change, the panel itself adds a system line — `Nozzle set to 0.6 mm` — with an `Undo` chip, so there's always an offer even when the agent proposes nothing. **Caveat:** I don't know whether undoing a printer change is implemented; if it isn't, the line should appear without the chip rather than offer something that fails.

## Where I don't have a better design

- **17 (project marked dirty), 13 and 14 (staged photo, duplicated message)** — these are defects with one correct behaviour, not design choices.
- **1's matching quality** — a search problem. My proposals only stop it being fatal; they don't make it good.
- **7 (connecting a printer)** — I can design where it's mentioned, but not what it does, because the app has nowhere for it to lead yet.
- **10 (keeping a thread on back)** — I have two designs and a preference, but the rule it bends is yours.
- **3's "Show all 13"** — I'm proposing the same in-panel picker as Move B, filtered by brand. If you'd rather the agent listed them in prose, I think that's worse at 320 px, but I don't have evidence, only judgement.

# Spike: identifying a printer from a photo

Second half of the printer-identification spike. The first half,
`../printer-naming/`, tested words; this one tests photos, alone and together
with a few words. Same approach: the whole packaged catalogue is in the prompt
and the model does the identifying.

## Layout

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `corpus.jsonl` | 15 cases: 12 photos alone, 3 photos with words |
| `instructions.txt` | photo prompt v1: the words prompt v2 plus a section on reading photos |
| `instructions.v2.txt` | photo prompt v2: adds rules on printed sizes, shape-only guesses and clones |
| `schema.json` | answer shape; adds `evidence`, what the model says it saw |
| `run.sh` | runs the corpus; `-i` picks the prompt, `-t` tags the run |
| `score.py` | scores one or more runs |
| `out/<run>/` | per case: the photo as attached, the prompt, the answer, the log |

The photos are **not** in the repo. They live in `~/Downloads/printer-photos/`
with `ground-truth.json` (source page, author, licence, expected answer). They
are Wikimedia Commons photos under CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA; the CC BY ones need
credit if they are ever published. `out/` holds copies, and `.gitignore` keeps
them out.

**The model can read an attachment's filename.** Codex sends each image with
its path as text, `<image name=[Image #1] path="...">`, using the path exactly
as passed on the command line; attached as `zebra-canary-7731.jpg` and asked,
the model quoted the name back. So each photo is copied under a random name
(`6d768f52812d.jpg`) and attached by that bare name from inside its folder: no
filename such as "Problemen met neptune 4 Max Elegoo.jpg", no run tag and no
case number reaches the model. `out/<run>/<case>.attached` records which random
name a case used. The chat in `../printer-naming/` does the same.

The photos' embedded metadata was checked with exiftool: none carries a title,
description or keyword naming the printer.

The first runs attached photos as `out/<run>/P09.jpg`; the spike was then
rerun with random names. Both sets are below.

## Running it

```bash
./run.sh -i instructions.v2.txt -t mine
./score.py gpt-5.6-terra-mine
```

To try a photo yourself, use the chat in `../printer-naming/`:

```
./run.sh
you> /photo ~/Downloads/printer-photos/08 - Voron 3D printer.jpg
you> the 300
```

## Results (2026-09-17, gpt-5.6-terra, three runs per prompt)

| | prompt v1 | prompt v2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pooled | 32/45 | 38/45 |
| model name or size printed on the machine (P01 P02 P04 P05 P06 P12) | 16/18 | 18/18 |
| shape only, no readable name (P03 P07 P09 P10 P11) | 4/15 | 8/15 |
| size can't be seen, must ask (P08) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| photo plus words (W01–W03) | 9/9 | 9/9 |

v2's gain is almost all two cases: the bed-label rule fixed the A1 bed close-up
(P05, 1/3 → 3/3), and the shape-only rule made the old Anycubic ask instead of
guessing (P10, 0/3 → 3/3).

**Resin printers were refused every time** (P12, W03: 12/12 across both
prompts), including when the words said "my elegoo" and pointed at Elegoo's
filament printers.

**No invented catalogue ids** in 90 calls.

### Rerun with random names

Same corpus, same two prompts, three runs each, photos attached by random
name. Case P05 was also corrected: the catalogue gives the Bambu P2S the same
256x256x256 build volume as the A1, so showing both and asking is right, and
the earlier expectation that allowed only the A1 was wrong. All eight runs are
scored against the corrected corpus.

| | v1, old names | v1, random | v2, old names | v2, random |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model name or size printed on the machine | 16/18 | 16/18 | 18/18 | 18/18 |
| shape only, no readable name | 4/15 | 5/15 | 8/15 | 5/15 |
| size can't be seen, must ask | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| photo plus words | 9/9 | 9/9 | 9/9 | 9/9 |
| **total** | **32/45** | **33/45** | **38/45** | **35/45** |
| failures that were a confident wrong answer | 8 | 7 | 4 | 3 |
| failures that asked for the label (recoverable) | 5 | 5 | 3 | 7 |

Nothing moved where a name or size is printed, or where words came with the
photo: those rows are identical across all 180 case-runs. The random names
changed nothing there, which is what the old names carrying no hint predicts.

The shape-only row moves between runs (8/15, then 5/15 on the same prompt),
so three runs are not enough to measure v2 against v1 on that row. What does
hold across both v2 sets is the kind of failure: on v1 most failures were a
confident wrong answer; on v2 most are a wrong shortlist followed by a request
for the model name on the label, which the person can answer.

### Where it fails

- **P03 — a P1S shot from above, lid off.** 1 of 3 on v2. Two runs called it an
  A1, a completely different machine, despite a box frame the A1 does not have.
- **P07 — a home-built Prusa MINI clone.** 0 of 3 on both prompts. It reads the
  machine as a Prusa i3 MK2, which is not packaged, and calls it unsupported.
  The MINI profile is what fits.
- **P09 — a Neptune 4 Max.** 1 of 3 on v2. It sees ELEGOO and a large open
  frame but guesses the Neptune generation wrong (3 Max, 3-family, 2-family).

### It sometimes reports evidence that is not in the photo

Checked by eye against the photos:

- P03, v2 run 1: says the bed reads "BUILD VOLUME 256 x 256 x 256". Nothing on
  that bed is legible from that angle. The v2 rule that a printed size is the
  strongest evidence probably invited this.
- P03, v1 run 1: describes an "open-frame bed-slinger layout" and a "large gray
  vertical gantry". The photo shows an enclosed box frame.
- P07, v2 run 2: says there is an embossed "Prusa i3 MK2" marking. The base is
  embossed with a partial "PRUSA MINI".

Everywhere a label really is visible — "K1C" and "BUILD VOLUME 220x220x250" on
the K1C, "X1-Carbon" on the X1C, "Bambu Lab A1" behind the cat, "ELEGOO MARS" —
it read it correctly, every run.

So `evidence` cannot be shown to the person as fact, and a rule that rewards
finding a label needs a counterweight ("if you cannot read it, say so").

### What this suggests for the product

A photo is reliable when it shows a name or a size, and unreliable when the
model has to judge by shape. So when a photo has no readable name, the
assistant should show its best two or three and ask for **a photo of the
label** — the nameplate, the sticker on the back, the screen's About page —
rather than a typed answer. That turns the weak case into the strong one.

### What the numbers do not cover

- 12 photos, one model, one day. Three runs per prompt.
- Two ground truths are uncertain: P10 (uploader says only "Anycubic i3") and
  P11 (uploader says only "Creality").
- The photos are Commons photos, which skew tidier than what people send from
  a phone mid-problem.

# Spike: identifying a printer from what someone types

Prototype for replacing `printer_catalog_search` — the keyword filter in
`OrcaPrinterBackend::search_catalog` that requires every word of the query to
appear in a printer's name — with the whole catalogue in the model's prompt.

The question this spike answers: **if you hand the model all 383 packaged
printer models and let it do the interpreting, how often does it get the right
printer?**

Words only. Photos are the next spike.

## Layout

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `build_catalog.py` | reads `resources/profiles/` and dumps one entry per model |
| `catalog.json` | 383 models: id, vendor, model, build volume, nozzles, material |
| `catalog.txt` | the compact form that goes in the prompt (~3,700 tokens) |
| `instructions.txt` | prompt v1 |
| `instructions.v2.txt` | prompt v2 — adds the prefix-ambiguity rule |
| `corpus.jsonl` | 50 test cases with expected outcomes |
| `schema.json` | JSON shape the model must answer in |
| `run.sh` | chat with the assistant yourself, or `--batch` to run the corpus |
| `turn.py` | chat-mode helper: builds each turn's case, prints the answer, keeps the history |
| `score.py` | scores a run against the corpus |
| `compare.py` | shows where repeat runs disagree |
| `instructions.v2r2.txt`, `instructions.v2r3.txt` | byte-identical copies of v2; the run is named after the instruction file, so repeats need their own copy |
| `out/<run>/` | per-case prompt, raw answer and log |

## Trying it yourself

```bash
./run.sh
```

Type what printer you have, the way a person would. Each answer shows what the
assistant said, the cards it would draw (with build volume and catalog id), and
whether it asked a question or called the printer unsupported. The conversation
carries across turns, so you can correct it ("no wait, the S1") or answer its
question ("the small one").

- `/photo PATH [words]` attaches a photo (the path may contain spaces); the
  chat uses the photo-aware prompt from `../printer-photos/` by default
- `/reset` starts a new conversation
- `/raw` toggles the model's raw JSON answer
- `/quit` leaves
- `-m <model>` and `-i <instructions file>` pick another model or prompt
  (default `gpt-5.6-terra` and `instructions.v2.txt`)

Every turn's full prompt and answer are kept in the temp folder printed at
start, for when you want to see exactly what the model was given. A card marked
`INVENTED ID` means the model named a printer that is not in the catalogue.

## Running the corpus

```bash
./run.sh --batch -j 8
./score.py gpt-5.6-terra-v2
```

`--batch` skips cases that already have a result, so delete `out/<run>/` to
redo one. The run is named after the model and the instructions file.

If the profiles change, rebuild the catalogue first:

```bash
./build_catalog.py ../../../../resources/profiles > catalog.json && python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('catalog.json'));open('catalog.txt','w').write(chr(10).join(f\"{e['catalogId']} | {e['buildVolume'] or '?'}\" for e in d))"
```

## The corpus

50 cases in nine shapes:

- **name-in-sentence** (9) — the real model name inside ordinary speech
- **ambiguous-partial** (8) — "bambu a1", where several models fit
- **clue-only** (7) — "the ender with the touchscreen", no model name at all
- **size-only** (6) — a bed size and nothing else
- **not-in-catalogue** (6) — resin printers, laser cutters, models we don't ship
- **typo** (6) — "ender3v2", "neptun 4 pro", "BAMBU LAB A1 MINI"
- **correction** (4) — a second turn that revises the first
- **non-english** (2) — Spanish and Chinese, including the Chinese brand name
- **junk** (2) — gibberish, and a question that isn't an identification

Each case declares the ids that must appear, the ids that may appear, a card
cap, and whether a question is required. Scoring is automatic except for the
prose, which needs reading.

The scorer's hardest check is **invented ids**: any catalogId not in
`catalog.json` is a fail, because it means a card that cannot be installed.

## Results (2026-09-17, gpt-5.6-terra via the `codex` CLI)

**Prompt v1 — 47/50.** Three failures, all the same mistake: when the query
exactly equals one model name but is also the start of others, it showed that
one model alone. "bambu a1" got the A1 without the A1 mini; "bambu x1" got the
X1 without the X1 Carbon; "ender 3" got the bare Ender-3 out of twelve.

**Prompt v2 — 50/50 on the first run.** v2 adds one rule: a query that starts
more than one model name is not a clear match even when it exactly equals one
of them. That rule alone fixed all three.

**Repeats of v2 partly blocked.** The Codex account hit its usage limit after
129 calls, so runs 2 and 3 completed only 15 and 14 of the 50 cases.

**Pooled across the three v2 runs — 78 passes, 1 failure in 79 case-runs.**
The one failure is "bambu x1" in run 3, which reverted to the v1 behaviour and
showed the X1 alone.

Of the 14 cases that completed in all three v2 runs, 11 gave identical answers.
All three that varied were partial-name cases (`prusa mini`, `ender 3`,
`bambu x1`). Two of the three varied harmlessly — the same cards, labelled
`ask` in one run and `propose` in another. One varied into a wrong answer.

**No invented catalog ids in any run.** That was the failure mode most worth
measuring and it did not occur once in 129 calls.

**A corpus bug the model caught.** Case E07 expected "snapmaker artisan" to be
unsupported. The Snapmaker Artisan is in fact packaged. The model was right and
the corpus was wrong; E07 is now a positive case.

**These runs used a catalogue with gaps.** The first version of
`build_catalog.py` did not follow the `inherits` chain in machine presets, so
63 of the 383 models went into the prompt with build volume `?` — the Bambu
Lab A1 and the Snapmaker Artisan among them. The app itself resolves
inheritance (`PrinterCatalog.cpp`, `resolve_machine`). The dump now does too,
leaving 9 unknown. Every result above was recorded with the gappy catalogue, so
the size-based cases were tested with less information than the app has. They
should be re-run.

### What the numbers do not cover

- Only one model was tested, on one day.
- Repeats cover 14 of 50 cases, weighted toward the first two shapes.
- Automatic scoring judges which cards were shown and whether a question was
  asked. It does not judge the prose; that was read by hand once.
- The catalogue here keys on `<vendor folder>/<model name>`, while
  `OrcaPrinterBackend` keys on `<vendor id>/<model id>`. Same one-per-model
  granularity, different spelling.
- 383 models are dumped here; the app counts 384. One model has no machine
  preset naming it, so this dump drops it.
- 9 models still have no build volume after resolving inheritance (six are
  Creality `_CFS-C` duplicates). Not chased.

content.text:
I read both spikes. They change the biggest part of my proposals: the search findings are no longer a UI problem to design around, because the spike shows the keyword filter can be removed entirely.

## What the spikes establish

- **Words:** put all 383 packaged models in the prompt and let the model identify. Prompt v2 scored 50/50 on the 50-case corpus, and 78 passes in 79 case-runs pooled, with no invented catalog ids in 129 calls. It handles typos ("ender3v2"), Spanish and Chinese, corrections on the next turn, size-only answers, and clue-only phrases.
- **Photos:** reliable when a name or a printed size is visible (18/18 on prompt v2), unreliable from shape alone (5–8 of 15, and it moves between runs). Resin printers were refused 12/12. The model sometimes reports reading a label that isn't legible in the photo.
- **Limits both READMEs state:** one model, one day; the word repeats covered 14 of 50 cases; the catalog used had 63 models with unknown build volume; the photos are tidy Wikimedia shots, not phone photos taken mid-problem.

## Proposals that change

**Findings 1, 2, 3, 21 (bad matching, wrong-vendor match, truncated results sold as complete, no result counts).** I proposed a scoring matcher plus a results block that shows "3 of 13" and a "Show all" chip. Drop most of that. The spike replaces `printer_catalog_search` with the catalog in the prompt, and all four findings dissolve at the source: there is no keyword result set to truncate, so there is no count to display and no "I found three matches" to contradict. What survives from my Move A is only the card layout — brand as its own line above the model, which still fixes the doubled names — and the community-profile label below.

**Finding 5 (no exit for an unlisted printer).** I proposed a standing "not finding it?" row after a failed search, triggered by heuristics. Better: the spike's schema has an explicit `unsupported` action. Bind the panel to it — when the answer is `unsupported`, the panel itself renders the exit ("Set it up myself", "Browse the full list") rather than leaving it to the agent's prose, which is where it kept getting lost. Same for `ask`: candidate cards plus the question, and **no** primary Add button, because the model is telling you it isn't sure.

**Finding 6 (no way to browse).** Partly solved without UI: the model now holds the whole list, so "show me the brands you support" is answerable. I'd still build the in-panel picker, but it drops from critical scaffolding to a convenience for people who prefer to point rather than type.

**Photo flow (finding 24 and the photo path generally).** My proposal was only about rendering. The spike gives the more valuable behaviour: when a photo has no readable name, don't ask for more words — ask for **a photo of the label**, and say where it is (the sticker on the back, the nameplate, the About page on the screen). That turns the weak case into the strong one. So the composer should offer a "Photo of the label" chip in exactly that state, next to the two or three candidate cards.

**Card "why this one" line.** I proposed showing the matching evidence on the card. Withdraw that for photos: the spike caught the model describing a bed label that isn't legible and an embossed name that says something else. Evidence from a photo can't be shown as fact. At most, phrase it as a claim the person can check ("looks like an enclosed box frame — is that right?"), and never quote a label the person can't verify in their own photo.

**Finding 12/18 (dead cards, docked button).** Unchanged in spirit, but now driven by the action word instead of guesswork: `propose` with one id → one live card with its own button; `propose` with two or three, or `ask` → cards with "This one" and no global Add; `unsupported` → no cards at all.

## Proposals that stand as they were

4 (no-agent state), 7 (connection promises — still a product gap, the spikes don't touch it), 8 (Printer settings… opening the Add flow), 9 (opener states the job and its end), 10 (keeping a thread on back — still your call), 11 (doubled names), 13, 14, 15 (approval card says what changes), 16 (confirmation after adding), 17, 19 (pinned card wording), 20 (clipped placeholder), 22 (empty bubbles), 25.

## What the spikes add that I hadn't proposed

- **Make the answer schema the UI contract.** `action` + `catalogIds` + `question` + `say` maps one-to-one onto panel states. Today the panel depends on the agent choosing to call `printer_propose` and `printer_suggest` in the right order; with the schema, the state is the answer.
- **Say "we don't slice resin" in its own words.** Resin printers were refused every time, correctly. That deserves distinct copy, not the generic "not in the list" — a person with a Mars needs to know it will never be in the list.
- **A rule that "I can't read it" is an acceptable answer,** as a counterweight to the rule that a printed size is the strongest evidence. The photo README says the second rule probably invited the invented label readings.

## Two gaps I'd close before trusting this

- **The x1c case is untested.** The word corpus has "bambu x1" but no query that a third-party profile could steal. The spike's catalog does contain `Orca Arena Printer/Orca Arena X1 Carbon` and `Chuanying/Chuanying X1`, so the trap exists in the data — it just isn't in the 50 cases. Worth adding "x1c", "my x1c", and "creality k1" as cases, and worth keeping my "community profile" label on the card either way.
- **"voron 2.4 350mm" isn't in the corpus either,** and that exact phrasing is the one that produced a false "unsupported" in the running app. Case G03 covers the bare "350" answer, not the glued unit.

ignore these gaps.  Now, put all the problems you into 5 categories:

1.  the problems that can be solved by changing mechanism to the one demonstrated in the spikes that I gave you.
2.  The problems that can be addressed by changing other back-hand mechanisms. 
3.  the problems that can be addressed by changing the frontend/UI elements or wording.
4.   The problems that can be addressed by other changes. 
5.  the puns that they don't have solutions for

Here are all 25 findings from the merged list, sorted into your five buckets. Where an item needs work in two places I've named the primary bucket and said what spills over.

## 1. Solved by the spike mechanism (catalog in the prompt, typed answer schema, photo rules)

- **F1 — ordinary phrasing gets a false "not found."** The keyword filter goes away; the model identifies from the full list. 50/50 on the word corpus.
- **F2 — wrong manufacturer stated as certain.** The prefix-ambiguity rule turns "several models fit" into showing two or three and asking, instead of one confident card. (A "community profile" label on the card is a UI addition on top.)
- **F3 — truncated results sold as complete.** There is no keyword result set left to truncate, so the false "I found three matches" cannot arise.
- **F21 — search quality invisible.** Dissolves with F3: nothing is being silently cut.
- **F5 — no exit for an unlisted printer.** The schema's `unsupported` action gives the panel a reliable trigger for the exit. (Drawing the exit is bucket 3.)
- **Photo behaviour that wasn't in my list but the spike settles:** when no name is readable, ask for a photo of the label rather than more words, and never tell apart sizes of one family by how big the machine looks.

## 2. Solved by other back-end changes

- **F4 — no-agent dead end.** The panel must render the embedded agent-setup page instead of a live-looking conversation; host wiring, with copy from bucket 3.
- **F8 — "Printer settings…" in Prepare opens the Add flow.** Routing: map the selected printer to a saved printer, and decide what happens when it is a shipped profile.
- **F11 — doubled printer names.** Name composition: display brand and model separately, save the model name alone.
- **F15 — the approval card says nothing.** The coordinator must hand the card a human summary ("0.4 mm → 0.6 mm on Bambu Lab A1 mini"); rendering it is bucket 3.
- **F17 — adding a printer marks the open project as modified.** Preset-switching side effect; no UI involved.
- **F10 — going back destroys the conversation.** Keeping the draft session alive is a host lifetime change. Whether to keep it at all is bucket 4.
- **F25 — no follow-up after a change.** A guaranteed system line is frontend, but an "Undo" chip needs a real inverse operation in the back end.

## 3. Solved by front-end or wording changes

- **F6 — no way to browse.** An in-panel brand → model picker. (The spike lets the model recite brands as a stopgap; at 320 px a picker is better.)
- **F9 — nothing states what the flow does or where it ends.** Two-line opener plus a caption under the pinned card.
- **F12 — rejected and superseded cards stay live.** Collapse them to a grey line and take their button away.
- **F16 — no confirmation after adding.** New card at the top, one dismissible strip naming what was added and what was assumed.
- **F18 — "tap the card" on inert cards.** Give every card its own button; if a docked button stays, it names its target.
- **F19 — pinned card jargon.** Plain values, "(assumed)" marks, a caption instead of four bare dashes. The values themselves arrive from the back end, so that side needs to send human names.
- **F20 — clipped placeholder.** One line, truncated with an ellipsis, shorter text.
- **F22 — empty agent bubbles.** No bubble until there is text; one named activity line while tools run.
- **F23 — "Set it up myself" unexplained.** Rename it, and open the picker in the panel instead of a floating dialog.
- **F24 — photo rendering.** Thumbnail inside the composer; the picture itself in the thread.
- **F13 — sent photo stays staged.** Clear it on send. A front-end state bug, unless staging turns out to be owned by the host.
- **F14 — message rendered twice.** A streaming or merge bug in the same area.

## 4. Solved by other kinds of change

- **F10's policy half.** "Every opening is a new session" versus "an accidental back shouldn't lose what I typed" is your product decision, not a mechanism.
- **Resin printers.** Correctly refused, but they need their own sentence rather than the generic "not in the list" — a copy decision plus a support-policy statement.
- **F7's larger half.** Wording can stop the agent promising to connect the printer, but making connection real is feature work: there is no Connect entry point in this build.

## 5. No solution I can offer

- **F7 beyond the wording.** I can design where connecting is mentioned, not what it does, because nothing in the app does it yet.
- **Shape-only photo identification.** The spike measures 5–8 of 15 and it moves between runs. Asking for a label photo routes around it; nothing I know of fixes it.
- **Run-to-run variance.** The spike saw 3 of 14 repeated cases answer differently, one of them wrongly. No interface removes that; it only decides how much a wrong answer costs, which is why the "ask" state must never carry a primary Add button.

Every other finding has a solution I'd stand behind.
for the problems solved by front-end or wording changes, do you think you can give the specs in text, or do you think we need figma design for them?

Text is enough for most of them. Four need a picture — and I don't think that picture has to be Figma.

## Text specs are enough (8 of 12)

These are wording or a one-line rule, and everything visual about them already comes from the token file:

- **F9 opener** — I can give the exact two sentences and the caption under the pinned card.
- **F19 pinned card** — exact row labels, the "(assumed)" suffix rule, and the mapping from preset names to human ones ("Bambu PLA Matte @BBL A1M" → "PLA Matte"). The layout already exists.
- **F20 placeholder** — one line, ellipsis, exact string.
- **F22 empty bubbles** — rule: no bubble until text arrives; one activity line named after the tool; it collapses on completion.
- **F23 rename** — "Set it up myself" → "Browse the full list", plus where it leads. (The thing it leads to is F6, which does need a picture.)
- **F13 staged photo cleared on send** and **F14 duplicate message** — defects with one correct behaviour, nothing to design.
- **F18 button placement rule** — "every card carries its own action; a docked button must name its target". The wireframe already shows the "This one" button, so this is a rule, not a new look.

## A drawing would prevent a bad guess (4 of 12)

- **F6 the browse picker.** A new surface with three levels (filter box → brands → models) in a 320 px column, with back navigation and a "my printer isn't listed" row. Too many layout decisions to leave in prose.
- **F12 + F18 card anatomy and its states.** One picture showing the same card live, as one of several candidates, and collapsed after being rejected or superseded. This is the centre of the flow and the states have to read at a glance.
- **F16 the after-add confirmation.** Where the strip sits relative to the list, what it says, how it dismisses, and the new card at the top.
- **F24 photos.** The staged thumbnail inside the composer and the sent image in the thread — both are size and position decisions.

## My recommendation on Figma

Don't go to Figma for these. ## ⚠ LESSON: the agent chat is a full, visible conversation — NEVER a one-line input
The user↔agent interaction is messy, multi-turn, back-and-forth, and often NOT cleanly
summarizable. ALWAYS show the ENTIRE chat history as a real scrollable conversation (the
dock), with the settled "Current setup" plan PINNED at the top as the artifact. Do NOT
collapse the conversation into a single input field, a one-line "refine…" box, or a tidy
changelog. The pinned plan is the source of truth for what will slice; the thread below it
is disposable exploration that stays fully visible. (Decided turns 3–4; regressed in turn 6.
Do not repeat.)

## Core conceptual model
- One app = a slicer. Home shows TWO concepts: **Projects** (your work; opens the Prepare
  screen) and **Printers** (your equipment: connection, model, filament/AMS colours,
  calibration, and a **Launch monitor** button). The monitor is a sub-window launched from a
  printer — never a co-equal app.
- Navigation = model **A**: one main window that navigates Home ⇄ Prepare/Check (+ Info) ⇄
  Printer config. Only monitor windows pop out (one per printer, many at once). Opening a
  second project REPLACES the first in the main window; you switch projects via Home. The
  ORCA logo / back control top-left returns to Home; projects auto-save.
- Ownership boundary: the USER supplies what is physically true, what the geometry MEANS, and
  the desired OUTCOME, and holds authority over consequential physical actions. The AGENT owns
  the ~247 invisible process settings (layers, walls, infill, speed, cooling, supports, seams…).
- Printer/filament/colour/model are FACTS ABOUT THE MACHINE → they live in Printer config. The
  project just POINTS at a printer via a loose picker (default: last-used / whatever's idle;
  changeable anytime, never a required first step). Colour INVENTORY = printer; colour→region
  MAPPING = project.
- Painting = annotate MEANING ("smooth face", "bearing surface", "screw hole", "no supports
  here"), and the agent DERIVES the modifiers — not user-set local wall counts / speeds.
- App-level presets/profiles/materials SHIP with the app; most users never touch them. They are
  discoverable only behind the "see all" door, when presets aren't enough. Do not give them
  prime real estate (fold into Preferences).

## Prepare-screen design principles
1. The agent is a SECOND input path, so every visible tool is an OPTIONAL accelerator — anything
   a tool does, you can also just ask for. Beginners talk; makers grab the tool.
2. The conversation is ALWAYS visible (see the lesson above): full history + pinned plan.
3. Four fixed zones, learned once: machine (top) · object on the plate (centre) · intent+plan
   conversation dock (right) · the one commit button, Slice (bottom).
4. Words/outcomes on the surface; numbers/parameters one "see all" layer down.
5. Depth opens as a dismissible layer over/beside the current context; the standing screen never
   permanently accumulates.

## Screen inventory
- **Home** — Projects + Printers.
- **Project window** (one main window, model A) with modes: **Prepare** (plate + tools + dock),
  **Check/Preview** (sliced paths, layer scrub, time/material, risks), **Info** (project
  knowledge: author, licence, safety, BOM, assembly, pictures, versions).
- **Printer config** — sections: Setup · Filament/AMS · Calibration · Maintenance & Privacy.
- **Monitor window** — pop-out per printer: camera, progress, temps, Pause/Resume/Stop, alerts.
- **Dialogs / overlays**: Send (preflight, one-way), the "see all" expert-settings layer,

  Multi-plate: "Print plate 2 ▾", menu has Slice/Print all plates + Export sliced file. Print always
  opens Send preflight.
- Printer chip = printer nickname · nozzle · plate · loaded spools as dots IN SLOT ORDER (never the
  project palette). Capped width, full names on hover. Mismatch = chip turns red and shows only the
  offending fact + inline fix; it's the only red thing in the header.
- Pinned card = YOU WANT (user's words, editable) · PLAN (agent's derived setup) · "Ready to check"
  until a valid slice exists, then time · material. No risk line on the card (dropped as too hard).
- No permanent toolbar: handles + strip (Place on face · Duplicate · Mark ▾ · ⋯) on selection only;
  ⋯ = mirror, cut, split, merge, text, measure, repair. Plate label at the plate's front edge shows
  what's on it and the colours used. Objects rail opens into a tree only when >1 object/plate/colour.
- Header = three zones: ‹ Home (left; no ORCA wordmark) · printer chip CENTRED · job button + ⋯ (right). No
  "Prints · x" chip in the header — print history lives on Home and in ⋯.
- Project name lives in the window title (Mac/Win); Linux shows it after Home. No dirty indicator.
- SUPERSEDED by turn 15 (below) — Printer chip click (turn 13) = popover, ~300px: a list of printers, one card each, EVERY card with
  its own settings ⚙ and monitor ↗ doors (never a shared door at the bottom). Chosen card expanded:
  full names · LOADED one row per slot in slot order ("used" marks the project's slots, ? = unknown
  spool, colour is a swatch only — printer sends hex not a name; remain % only for tagged Bambu
  spools). Others collapsed with status; click body to switch. "+ Add a printer" last. Non-Bambu
  printers have no live data: show configured values labelled "as set up". Read-only; no colour→slot
  mapping here. Red state adds a top block with the
  mismatch + two fixes; one mismatch at a time, worst first (offline > nozzle > plate > filament).
- Wireframes for this: `Orca Prepare Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 12+).

## Printer + spool chip (decided turn 15) — replaces the turn-12 chip and turn-13 popover
- ONE chip, TWO halves, parent → child: left = printer nickname · nozzle; right (nested, lighter
  ground, same outline) = colour dot · spool name. No plate on the chip. Slot dots only when the
  printer has slots (AMS / MMU). The chip NEVER turns red — it states facts; mismatches go to the
  thread + pinned card status row (retires 12c's red chip). Hover lifts one half and shows full names.
- Spool menu (right half): title "SPOOLS ON <printer>"; spools the person has used on this printer,
  last-used order, current ✓; click row = swapped, closes (2 clicks). Rare actions (change colour,
  rename, tune with the agent, reset tuning, filament settings, remove) only via ⋯ on hover/right-click.
  Last row "Other spool…" = search every preset that fits printer+nozzle → colour pick → prefilled
  name → "Use this spool" (adds to list). Quiet escapes: Generic preset… · Import a preset file….
- Printer menu (left half), one-printer = 5 lines: name + state (dot + word; ↗ monitor when connected)
  · Nozzle ▸ · Plate ▸ · Printer settings… · Add a printer…. Not connected shows one grey sub-line
  ("Prints go to a card. Connect…"). Multi-printer adds ONE middle section "OTHER PRINTERS" (state,
  ⚙ ↗ per row, click = switch). No fleet UI for one-printer people.
- Add a printer = 3 questions: 1 brand · model · nozzle (everyone's path; network finds listed under it
  as a shortcut — Bambu only via SSDP — picking one prefills the model and asks for the LAN access code
  or sign-in) · 2 plate · 3 "What spool is on it right now?" (same picker). Row clicks advance; Next
  only where several fields exist. Klipper/Moonraker/PrusaLink addresses go in later via the printer
  menu's Connect…. No filament page.
- AMS chip label = what the project prints with (✓ row), never slot 1: one spool → its name; several →
  "N spools", every used slot dot ringed.
- AMS: spool half = chosen spool name + slot dots; menu top section = slots as reported (swatch, plastic,
  % for tagged Bambu only; Unknown → Identify…); remembered spools below. Klipper MMU: same, from the
  gate map, footer says so, no %. After a swap: chip, PLAN material word, one grey system line in the
  thread; the chat never changes the selection.
- Tokens: JusPrin light/dark set (from the brief) applies at hi-fi; wireframes stay lo-fi.

## Add a printer — after testing (turn 20, PROPOSED, not decided)
- Hands-on test of the built app: first-time user didn't know the job or its end, couldn't browse, got a
  confident wrong printer from a nickname, was told a listed printer was unsupported, was told to "tap
  the card" when it couldn't be tapped. 19b stays the placement; turn 20 replaces panel STATES only.
- Identification from the full printer list, answering in THREE shapes the panel draws itself:
  PROPOSE (one card, red "Add this printer" ON the card bottom-right, "Not this one" quiet chip under the
  assumptions sentence, no Add docked at the panel foot) · ASK (2–3 cards each with its own "This one",
  question in one sentence beneath, NO red Add anywhere; manufacturer card before COMMUNITY PROFILE ·
  Orca Arena) · UNSUPPORTED (one agent sentence + a panel-drawn two-row exit block: Browse the full list ·
  Set it up myself; resin printers get one sentence, no exit block).
- Opener = ONE agent message: job + end ("connecting comes later") + question; then the photo tip; a
  "Browse the full list" chip; network rows. Composer placeholder on one line, ellipsised. "assumed" is
  explained where it first appears (PROPOSE), not in the pinned card.
- Cards: brand on its own small uppercase line, model bold beneath, build volume; rejected/superseded
  cards collapse to one grey line, no button; one live card at a time. Grey activity line "Looking
  through the printer list…" while the agent works, gone when the reply lands.
- Two manual doors, two fixed labels EVERYWHERE: "Browse the full list" (in-panel brands → models, with
  counts, filter, pictures + build volume; picking a model returns to chat as PROPOSE) and "Set it up
  myself" (the ConfigWizard page, 18e, prefilled) — last row of the models list and second row of the
  exit block. Header door of the Add panel = "Browse the full list" (replaces "Set it up myself").
- Photos: staged = 48px thumbnail INSIDE the composer above the text line, ×, file name, "add a note, or
  just send", explicit ↑; sent = the picture itself is the user's message (~120px) with caption, composer
  empty; no readable name → ASK + "I can't read a model name…" + chip "Photo of the label" (same picker).
  Shape-only guesses never PROPOSE.
- After Add: printers column returns, new card on TOP highlighted once, dismissible strip above the list
  ("<model> added · nozzle, plate, filament — assumed · Not connected yet · Change" → 19b). Saved name =
  model name alone ("Bambu Lab A1 mini", second one "… 2"). No Connect… link in the test app because
  connecting isn't built; the DECIDED design (15g/18) keeps Connect… — not a design change.
- Change confirmation card: title "Change nozzle" · "0.4 mm → 0.6 mm on <printer>" · consequence in
  words · buttons name the OUTCOME ("Set 0.6 mm" / "Keep 0.4 mm"), never Approve/Reject, no tool name.
  After: Nozzle row "0.6 mm · changed" (red), card collapses to grey line, system line "Nozzle set to
  0.6 mm". OPEN: whether a physical fact the user stated needs confirming at all.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 20.

## Printer conversation placement (turn 19 — EXPLORATION, undecided)
- VOCABULARY (user asked): "conversation panel" = the Prepare-screen agent column (thread + input,
  pinned card where one applies), attached to the window edge, never a modal. "printers column" = the
  PRINTERS strip on Home (5b). Avoid the coined words "dock" and "cabinet" in labels from now on.
- Six placements for a freeform printer thread (Add + Change), each with a pinned facts card unless the
  UI itself is the artifact: 19a modal chat · 19b printers column becomes the conversation panel · 19c
  main window navigates to Printer config with a conversation panel (config page = the artifact, no
  pinned card) · 19d permanent conversation panel on Home, cards carry state · 19e printer card expands
  into its own thread · 19f = 18b first, correction field grows into a thread on demand. Agent lean:
  19c (+19f's reveal).
- Thread rules (Ken, turn 19 comments): every opening is a NEW session (no carried history); the AGENT
  opens the thread saying what it can do here; chips are specific actions ("Use 0.3 mm layers"), never
  bare Yes/No, and the open input always sits beneath them; a panel header label names where ‹ leads
  ("Printers"), not the current item.
- 19b·Add (Ken): the Add flow in the panel must carry ALL of 18's information in chat form: opener lists
  words / photo / network finds in the FIRST agent message; camera icon in the input row on every screen;
  recognised = 18b card + assumptions line + "Add this printer" primary chip; ambiguous = 18d; network
  = 18c. Photo upload must be discoverable and possible in every thread: a LABELLED "Photo" button LEADS the
  composer (leading-edge attach, as chat apps do, but labelled because it's a primary path), whole panel is
  a drop zone; a photo never auto-sends — removable thumbnail above the composer, optional words, explicit
  send (thumbnail INSIDE the composer box, above the text line); the sent photo shows in the thread as the
  user's message. No dashed drop card (looked like a candidate card, vanished after turn one): the agent's
  opener says how in words. Composer placeholders are a likely ANSWER to the agent's last message; on the first
  turn that is an example answer to the opener ("e.g. bambu a1 mini or not sure, the small one"), never
  "type…". The photo path is a separate, styled TIP paragraph under the opener (red left rule, camera). Primary chips = chip shape, red fill.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` turn 19.

## Add a printer (decided turn 18; 16 and 17 REJECTED — no chat window, no pinned card)
- LESSON: don't convert wizard steps into a chat. The agent's value is (a) recognising the printer
  from ANY evidence — loose words, a dropped photo of the printer/nameplate/box, or what the network
  reports — and (b) knowing what NOT to ask: nozzle/plate/filament get stated defaults, corrected
  later in the Prepare chip (15a) or the project conversation. Setup settles ONE fact.
- Home = 5b. "+ Add printer" → small dialog: "What printer do you have?" free-text field + drop-a-photo
  + FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK rows ("Use this") + small link "Set it up myself" (ConfigWizard, unchanged).
- Recognised → ONE card (profile picture + name) + one line "I'll assume 0.4 mm nozzle, the textured
  PEI plate it ships with, and PLA. If different, tell me here or in your first project" + one
  correction field + Not this one / Add this printer. Correction redraws the card; no thread.
- "Use this" on a network find (Bambu SSDP, Klipper/PrusaLink mDNS) → the SAME 18b screen, card
  filled from what the printer reported (nozzle, plate, AMS slots); sentence says nothing is assumed;
  one optional access-code field; Not this one / Add this printer (Add connects when a code is given).
- Ambiguous words → the agent states what tells the candidates apart, shows 2–3 picture cards, offers
  a photo as the shortcut, and KEEPS the text field (tap, photo or more words all answer); "not in the
  list" → wizard custom-printer page, prefilled.
- After Add: cabinet card on top ("as set up"/connected) + dismissable STARTER MODELS row.
- Manual path (18e) = "Set it up myself" link in 18a or "not in the list" in 18d → the dialog body
  becomes the existing ConfigWizard printer page, unchanged, with a header link "Ask the agent
  instead"; whatever the agent inferred is pre-ticked.
- No agent set up (18f) = 18a's layout with the text field replaced by 8a's connect card (title "No
  agent connected" · one-sentence nudge about THIS screen only · red "Set up the agent" → 9c ·
  sub-line; no disabled input).
  Network finds and "set it up myself" still work without an agent; on return the dialog becomes 18a.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 18; 17 kept dimmed for reference).

## Add a printer (turn 17 — REJECTED, kept for history)
- Home = 5b (projects gallery + printer cabinet). "+ Add printer" opens a MODAL DIALOG over Home with
  ONE question: "Let the agent guide me" (leads) · "Set it up myself". The pick REPLACES the dialog body
  in place: agent → a chat window (header link "Set it up myself instead" · ×; PINNED "New printer"
  card Printer · Nozzle · Plate · Filament shown empty up front, fills as facts settle; thread beneath;
  one input); self → OrcaSlicer's existing ConfigWizard printer dialog UNCHANGED (vendor, model grid
  with pictures + nozzle ticks, Filaments, Bed shape/Firmware for custom; Back/Next/Finish) plus a
  header link "Ask the agent instead". Switching either way carries settled facts; never asked twice.
  No agent set up → agent card greyed "Set up the agent first" (9c), form card leads. Never turn the
  cabinet column into a panel.
- Questions in order, each with its default as the first (bold) tap chip: which printer (words →
  profile match → picture card "This one?"; 2–3 fits → 2–3 cards; "I don't know" → where to look +
  brand chips; not in list → custom profile, bed then firmware, one question at a time, pinned card
  swaps rows) → nozzle ("Most printers ship with 0.4. Did you change it?", only sizes that exist) →
  filament ("Most people start with PLA", brand/colour optional, mapped to a shipped profile else
  Generic) → plate (only if the profile lists >1) → confirm line = pinned card read aloud → Done.
  Settled facts appear as grey ✓ lines in the thread. Connecting is NOT part of setup (printer menu's
  Connect…); the panel says so once.
- Done closes the dialog → cabinet shows the new card on top ("as set up", Connect… link) and a
  dismissable STARTER MODELS row for that printer above the projects; opening one = new project → Prepare.
- Wireframes: `Orca Printer Setup Wireframes.dc.html` (turn 17+).

## Visual system
Modernist design system (flat, Archivo, red #ec3013 on light, 2px rules, 0 radius). The working
files are LO-FI wireframes (Kalam sketch font) — options canvases, newest turn on top, ids like
6a/6b. `Orca Home Wireframes.dc.html` holds turns 1–6; `Orca Agent Wireframes.dc.html` holds 7–11
(dock, unconfigured state, agent setup and after); `Orca Agent Wireframes 2.dc.html` holds 14+. Start a new page when one grows past ~5 turns.
Hi-fi in Modernist comes later.
