You're partly right. It's not the tools telling the model what to do, though — it's the app's code telling the model what to do, and most of that design is mine.

**Where the model does use judgment.** It reads your words or photo, decides which printer it is or whether to ask, and writes its own reply. When it offers something like "Use 0.3 mm layers", it chose that itself; the tool only draws the button. That part works the right way round.

**Where the roles really are reversed.** In three places the app already knows the answer, but orders the model to deliver it:

- **You tap "This one" or pick a printer from the browse list.** The app knows exactly which printer you chose. Instead of drawing the card, it sends the model the instruction "Call printer_identify to propose that printer alone", waits a full round trip, and has the model hand the decision back.
- **You tap "Use this" on a network printer.** The app has a direct lookup from the printer's reported model to the catalog. It asks the model to "find that model on the printer list" instead.
- **Scripted buttons.** The instructions dictate exact buttons: "call printer_suggest with one action 'Photo of the label'", "offer an Undo chip". The model is just relaying buttons the app could draw itself — the app knows when a photo had no readable name, and it knows the old nozzle size.

**Who designed it.** Mostly me:
- My first handoff asked for "suggestion chips … that send a typed action when clicked". That's where `printer_suggest` came from.
- My fix handoff said "replace `printer_propose` with one tool whose arguments are the spike's answer shape, so the panel's state *is* the answer". That made the model's tool call the route for drawing everything.
- I specified the "Photo of the label" button and the Undo button in the fix handoff and in the prompt for Claude Design, without saying the app should draw them.

The coding agent followed that faithfully. The round trips after "This one", "Use this" and browse picks were its own choice, but they follow from my rule that the model's answer drives the panel.

**The right split:**
- **The model:** identifying a printer from messy words or a photo, deciding what to ask, and saying things in its own words. That's the only part that needs intelligence.
- **The app:** everything it already knows. Draw the card when you pick a printer, match a network printer to its model, show Undo after a change, and keep photo access on the Photo button. It then tells the model what happened, so the model can answer follow-up questions.
- **Tools:** `printer_identify` shrinks to "which printer ids, and propose, ask or not-supported" — the one thing the app can't compute. `printer_change` stays. `printer_suggest` goes, unless you want the model to keep offering its own buttons like "Use 0.3 mm layers"; if it stays, the app never scripts its labels.

Should I write that up as a correction to the handoff for the coding agent?

Let's make sure you understand what actually need to happen. Describe your design in terms of what roles that ALM plays and what tools it needs to play that role properly. Use plain English under 200 words.

The model has two jobs. Everything else belongs to the app.

**Job 1: work out which printer someone has** (adding a printer). The model reads what the person typed, or their photo, and matches it against the full printer list, which the app puts in its instructions at the start. It asks a question when it isn't sure, and says so when the printer isn't supported. It needs one tool, `printer_identify`, to report its answer — which printer or printers, or "not supported" — so the app can draw the cards.

**Job 2: apply a change the person describes** (changing a printer). "I put a 0.6 nozzle on it" becomes a nozzle change. It needs one tool, `printer_change`, which asks the person to approve before anything is saved.

**Everything else is the model talking in its own words:** explaining, asking, suggesting. No tool.

**The app handles everything it already knows,** without asking the model:
- drawing the card when someone taps "This one", uses a network printer, or picks from the browse list;
- the Add button, Undo, the Photo button, and browsing.

Afterwards the app tells the model what happened, so it can answer follow-up questions.

So each mode gets exactly one tool, and `printer_suggest` goes away.

Tell me how LM interact with these two tools to get a job done. What input it gives to these two tools and what output and how it uses the output to get the job done.  demonstrate how this interaction means the intelligence happens within the ALM, not the tools.

The model does all the reasoning, and the two tools only do what a model can't do reliably. `printer_identify` checks the model's answer against the real printer list and draws it. `printer_change` saves a change after the person approves it. Each tool's output is a fact or an error that the model then reasons about.

## `printer_identify` (adding a printer)

**What the model sends:** its conclusion — which printer ids, and whether it's sure (propose), unsure (ask), or the printer isn't supported. Plus any nozzle size the person mentioned.
**What comes back:** "shown" if every id is on the list and the nozzle exists for that model; otherwise an error that says what's wrong.

| The person says | The model's reasoning | Tool call | Tool's part |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "the small bambu one" | Bambu's small model is the A1 mini, 180 mm | propose `A1 mini` | Checks the id exists, draws the card |
| "voron 2.4 350mm" | "350mm" means the 350 size | propose `Voron 2.4 350` | Same. No word matching; the model read it |
| "the ender with the touchscreen" | From its own knowledge: the V3 SE and V3 KE both have one | ask `V3 SE`, `V3 KE` | Draws two cards; the model writes the question in its reply |
| A photo | Reads the frame and any label | propose, or ask when nothing is readable | Same |

**How the model uses the output:** "shown" → it writes its reply ("That's the A1 mini — I'll assume…"). An error such as "the A1 mini ships 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm nozzles, not 0.25" is a fact it didn't have. It corrects itself or asks the person which size.

## `printer_change` (changing a printer)

**What the model sends:** the change it worked out, e.g. `nozzle: 0.6`.
**What comes back:** after the person taps "Set 0.6 mm", the printer as it now is. Or "rejected", or why it failed (e.g. no 0.6 profile for that model).

| The person says | The model's reasoning | Tool call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "i put a 0.6 nozzle on it" | The nozzle size changed | `nozzle: 0.6` |
| "swapped to a hardened steel 0.4" | The size didn't change; the material isn't tracked | None. It explains that |
| "the plate is smooth PEI now" | The plate belongs to each project, not the printer | None. It says where to change it |

**How the model uses the output:** "applied" → it confirms, and may suggest in its own words ("with 0.6 you can print thicker layers"). "Rejected" → it leaves things as they were. "Failed" → it passes on the reason.

## When the app already knows the answer

When the person taps "This one", picks from the browse list, or uses a network printer, the app draws the card itself. It then adds a line to the conversation saying what happened, and the model reads that line only so it can answer follow-up questions.

Here is what `printer_identify` sends back to the model for that example. I built it from the code rather than a live run, so the parts in `<…>` are placeholders I can't fill in without running it. The app serialises the result compactly with its keys in alphabetical order:

```json
{"actionId":"<id of this tool call>","result":{"action":"ask","shown":2},"state":"succeeded","workspace":{<the whole open project's state>},"workspaceRevision":<number>}
```

- **`"result":{"action":"ask","shown":2}`** — the tool's own output ([PrinterConversation.cpp:476](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:476)). It repeats back what the model sent ("ask") and how many cards were drawn. It gives the model nothing new.
- **`"state":"succeeded"`** — no approval step, because this tool is exempt from the approval card.
- **`"workspace":{…}` and `"workspaceRevision"`** — added to every tool result by the shared agent code ([AgentHost.cpp:1836](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1836)). The printer panel is wired to the open project's workspace, so every printer tool result carries the project's plates, objects, selection, slice estimates and setting changes. None of that has anything to do with adding a printer. The printer session turns the project off in its opening context (`include_workspace = false`), but the tool results bring it back on every call.

So for this call, the only thing the model learns is that its answer was accepted. The only case where the tool gives it real information is an error, such as a printer id that isn't on the list or a nozzle size that model doesn't ship.

**Two corrections to my previous message:**
- **The printer facts were made up.** I said the Ender-3 V3 SE and V3 KE "both have" a touchscreen, presented as the model's own knowledge. I didn't check that. Treat it as a made-up illustration, not a fact.
- **Two of the model's inputs are ignored.** It would send `"say"` and `"question"` alongside the ids, and the code never reads either. The question the person sees is the model's separate chat reply.
Tell me how you designed the input and output schemer for this tool and how you made it clear that the intelligence doesn't belong within the tool.

I didn't design it — I copied it, and I never made that point clear.

**Where the shape came from.** The spike asked the model for its whole reply as one JSON object: `action`, `catalogIds`, `question`, `say`. There, `say` was the text shown to the person, and the schema was the format of the model's final answer, not a tool. In the fix handoff (WP1, item 4) I wrote "replace `printer_propose` with one tool whose arguments are the spike's answer shape, so the panel's state *is* the answer". That turned an answer format into a tool's input without asking what a tool is for.

**What followed from that:**
- **`say` and `question` became dead fields.** In a tool call the model also writes its own chat reply, so they duplicated it, and the code never reads them.
- **I never designed an output.** I specified no output at all. The coding agent filled the gap with `{"action", "shown"}`, which just repeats back what the model sent.
- **The tool became a drawing channel, not a source of facts.** "The panel's state is the answer" made the tool the route for drawing the panel. Once the tool meant "draw this", app code started ordering the model to call it ("Call printer_identify to propose that printer alone"). That's the inversion you spotted.

**What a deliberate design looks like:**
- **Input — only the model's decision:** up to three printer ids, and whether it's sure, unsure, or the printer isn't supported (and why). No prose fields.
- **Output — facts the model can't know reliably, which it needs for its next sentence:**
  - for each printer: brand, model and build volume;
  - the nozzle sizes it ships;
  - the plate and filament the app will assume;
  - whether the person already has that printer.

  Errors teach the next call, and there's no project workspace in the result.
- **Description, stating the split in so many words:** "You decide which printer this is. This tool checks your ids against the catalog and returns the facts to state; it never chooses."

**The previous answer, in plain English**

- **"Not supported" comes off the tool.** Nothing about it can be checked against the list; it was only there to tell the panel when to show the "Set it up myself" and "Browse the list" buttons. Instead, those two buttons stay visible all the time, just above the text box, and the model says in its own words when it can't find a printer or when it's a resin printer.
- **The number of printers the model sends says how sure it is.** One printer means it's sure, and the card offers "Add this printer". Two or three mean it's unsure, and each card offers "This one". If it has no idea yet, it just asks and doesn't call the tool.
- **Why at most three:** it came from the test and the wireframes; nobody measured it. The panel is narrow, three picture cards fill it, and more than three means the model should ask a narrowing question instead.

**What details, and where they come from**

They're all in OrcaSlicer's printer profile files, which ship with the app. The app reads them once when the panel opens (`PrinterCatalog.cpp`), so the tool just looks them up:

| Detail | Where it's stored |
| --- | --- |
| Brand | The brand's file, e.g. `resources/profiles/Prusa.json` (its `name`) |
| Model name, nozzle sizes, plate it ships with, filament list | The model's file, e.g. `resources/profiles/BBL/machine/Bambu Lab A1 mini.json`: `nozzle_diameter`, `default_bed_type`, `default_materials` |
| Build volume | Worked out from each nozzle size's machine settings (`printable_area`, `printable_height`) |
| Picture | `<Model>_cover.png` in the brand's folder |

**Two catches, from checking the files and the code:**
- **The plate is usually missing.** Only 34 of 359 printer models say which plate they ship with; the Bambu A1 mini does, the Prusa MK3S doesn't. For most printers the tool would have no plate to give, and the model must not invent one. That's why the Plate row was blank for the Prusa in testing.
- **The "default filament" isn't necessarily PLA.** It's just the first entry in the model's list. For the Prusa MK3S that's "Prusa Generic ABS". Today the pinned card shows "PLA" regardless, while the printer is saved with the file's first filament. So a newly added MK3S may default to ABS while the card said PLA. **What the model does when more than three printers match**

It knows how many match because it's the one doing the matching — the whole printer list is in its instructions. The instructions then tell it what to do. Today they say:

> "ender 3" begins twelve model names … Show the ones that fit, up to three, and ask what separates them.

So with twelve matches the model picks three and asks. That's the "three Prusas" problem from testing in a new form: the person sees three of twelve and can reasonably assume that's all of them.

The rule I'd write instead:
- **Two or three fit:** show them as cards and ask what tells them apart.
- **More than three fit:** show no cards. Ask one question that narrows it down, naming what to look for — "The Ender 3 comes in twelve versions. What does the label on the front say — V2, V3, S1…?" — or point to "Browse the list".
- **If the model sends more than three anyway:** the tool refuses with an error saying exactly that, so the model corrects itself on the next try.

**JSON or plain text: JSON.** For example:

```json
{"printers":[{"id":"<catalog id>","brand":"Prusa","model":"MK3S","buildVolume":"250 × 210 × 210 mm",
  "nozzles":[0.25,0.4,0.6,0.8],"assumed":{"nozzle":0.4,"plate":null,"filament":"<first filament in the profile>"},
  "alreadyYours":false}]}
```

The reasons:
- **"Unknown" is explicit.** `"plate": null` tells the model there is no plate to mention. In prose, a missing fact is just absent, and the model tends to fill the gap — which is how a plate gets invented.
- **Exact values to quote.** The model copies "250 × 210 × 210 mm" or "0.25, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8" instead of paraphrasing a sentence.
- **It can be checked.** Every other tool in the app returns JSON, and the shared code can check a JSON result against its declared shape and test it. Prose can't be checked that way.
- **The cost is small.** Three printers with about eight fields each is a few hundred characters.

# The printer panel's two agent tools

Status: design, 2026-09-18. Not built. Supersedes the tool shapes in `printer-panel-fixes-handoff.md` WP1 (on branch `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`) and the tools in commit `0e55c4f9be`.

The printer panel on Home lets a person add a printer or change one they already have, by talking to the in-app agent. This document fixes who does what. **The model does the understanding. The app does everything it can already work out itself.** The model gets exactly two tools, one per mode. Each tool checks the model's decision against the real printer data, carries it out, and hands back facts the model needs for its next sentence. A tool never decides anything.

Paths are relative to the repo root. `J/` is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

---

## 1. The split

| Who | Does what |
| --- | --- |
| **The model** | Works out which printer the person has, from words or a photo. Works out what changed on a printer the person already has. Asks when it isn't sure. Explains, answers questions and suggests, in its own words. |
| **The app** | Everything it already knows: drawing a card when the person taps a printer, picks one from the browse list, or uses a network printer (matched by the model id the printer reports); the Add button; Undo after a change; the Photo button; the browse list; the always-visible "Browse the list · Set it up myself" doors. After each of these, the app adds one line to the conversation saying what happened, so the model can answer follow-ups. The app never tells the model which tool to call. |
| **`printer_identify`** (Add mode only) | Checks the printers the model named against the catalog, draws their cards, returns the facts to state. |
| **`printer_change`** (Change mode only) | Checks the change the model worked out against what this printer's profile allows, asks the person to confirm it, saves it, returns the printer as it now is. |

Retired: `printer_catalog_search`, `printer_propose`, `printer_suggest`. Suggestions are the model's words. Buttons the app can derive (Undo, Photo of the label, the manual-setup doors) are the app's.

### Rules for both tools

- Each mode offers **only its own tool**. Offering all tools in both modes let a Change conversation call the identify tool and clear the pinned card of an existing printer.
- **No project data in results.** Today every tool result carries the open project's whole workspace (plates, objects, selection, estimates, setting changes; `AgentHost::continue_after_tool`, `J/Agent/AgentHost.cpp` around line 1836). A printer session has nothing to do with the project. Its results carry only the tool's own result.
- **JSON results.** Unknown values are explicit `null`, so the model states nothing rather than filling a gap. Values are quotable as-is. Results are checkable against the declared output shape and testable, like every other tool in the app.
- **Errors say what to do next.** Every refusal names the problem and the facts needed to correct it.
- **No credentials through the model.** A printer's access code never appears in a tool's input or in the conversation (see 3.4).
- **No `planId`.** Neither tool joins grouped approvals; remove the field the shared registry adds to every change tool.
- **The description states the split** in the model's terms (quoted in 2.1 and 3.1).

---

## 2. `printer_identify`

### 2.1 What the model is told

At the start of every Add session, in the instructions:

- The whole printer list, one line per model: `<catalogId> | <build volume>`, built from `PrinterCatalog` (`J/PrinterSetup/PrinterCatalog.cpp`). The Orca Arena bundle is left out (Kenneth, 2026-09-17). About 15 KB, roughly 3,700 tokens, paid on the first request of each Add conversation.
- The rules, adapted from `agent-docs/jusprin/spikes/printer-naming/instructions.v2.txt` and `spikes/printer-photos/instructions.v2.txt`:
  - One printer fits: call the tool with it.
  - Two or three genuinely fit: call the tool with all of them, and ask in your reply what tells them apart.
  - **More than three fit: do not call the tool.** Ask one question that narrows it down and say where to look ("The Ender 3 comes in twelve versions. What does the label on the front say?"), or point to "Browse the list". Never show three of many.
  - A query that is the start of several model names is not a clear match, even when it equals one of them.
  - Nothing fits, or it isn't a filament printer (resin, laser): say so in one sentence. Do not call the tool. The panel's doors are always visible.
  - A photo: name a model only from a readable name or printed size; by shape alone, ask for a photo of the label. Never quote a label as read unless asking the person to confirm it.

Tool description:

> You decide which printer this is. This tool checks the printers you name against the app's printer list, shows them to the person, and returns the details to mention. It never picks a printer.

### 2.2 Input

```json
{ "catalogIds": ["<id>", "..."],   // 1 to 3, copied from the printer list
  "nozzle": 0.6 }                   // optional, mm, only when the person or a photo said so
```

Nothing else. The count carries the model's certainty: one id means sure (the card offers "Add this printer"); two or three mean unsure (each card offers "This one"). No `action`, `say`, `question`, `reason`, `plate`, `filament` or `provenance`: the model's words go in its reply, and "not supported" is not a tool call.

### 2.3 Output

```json
{ "printers": [
    { "catalogId": "<id>",
      "brand": "Prusa",
      "model": "MK3S",
      "buildVolume": "250 × 210 × 210 mm",
      "nozzles": [0.25, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
      "assumed": { "nozzle": 0.4, "plate": null, "filament": "<see 2.4>" },
      "alreadyYours": false } ] }
```

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `brand` | The brand's file, `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json`, its `name` |
| `model` | The model's file, `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/machine/<Model>.json`, with the brand not repeated |
| `buildVolume` | The machine settings for each nozzle size (`printable_area`, `printable_height`), following `inherits` |
| `nozzles` | The model file's `nozzle_diameter` |
| `assumed.nozzle` | What the person said, else 0.4 when the model ships 0.4, else the model's first size |
| `assumed.plate` | The model file's `default_bed_type`; **`null` when absent** (325 of 359 models have none) |
| `assumed.filament` | See 2.4 |
| `alreadyYours` | Whether one of the person's saved printers is this model |

The model uses the output to write its reply from facts ("I'll assume a 0.4 mm nozzle and PLA; this profile doesn't say which plate it ships with"), never from memory.

### 2.4 Errors

| Code | When | Message carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unknown_printer` | An id is not on the list | The id; "copy it exactly from the printer list" |
| `too_many` | More than three ids | "Ask one question that narrows it down instead" |
| `unknown_nozzle` | The stated nozzle isn't one the model ships | The sizes it ships |

### 2.5 Approval

None. The tool saves nothing; the person's tap on "Add this printer" is the decision.

### 2.6 Open for Kenneth

- **Which filament to assume.** Today the pinned card says "PLA" while the printer is saved with the first entry of the model's `default_materials`. For the Prusa MK3S that entry is "Prusa Generic ABS" (read from the code, not run). Proposal: the first PLA in that list, else the first entry, and the card shows what is actually saved.

---

## 3. `printer_change`

### 3.1 What the model is told

At the start of every Change session, in the instructions, the printer as it is now:
- name, brand and model;
- current nozzle, **and the nozzle sizes this model ships**;
- the loaded spools as a list (name, material, colour), not a summary;
- whether it is connected.

Today the model gets a one-line summary and not the nozzle sizes, so it learns them only from an error.

The rules: work out what physically changed from what the person says. Change only what they said changed. The plate belongs to each project, not the printer; say where to change it and don't call the tool. A nozzle material (hardened steel) isn't tracked; say so. Connecting isn't possible from this panel.

Tool description:

> You work out what changed on this printer from what the person says. This tool checks it against what this printer's profile allows, asks the person to confirm, saves it, and returns the printer as it now is. It never decides what changed.

### 3.2 Input

```json
{ "nozzle": 0.6,                       // optional, mm
  "spools": [                          // optional; the complete list as it is now
    { "name": "Teal PLA", "material": "PLA", "colour": "#2a9d8f" } ] }
```

At least one field. `spools` replaces the whole list, so the model restates every spool; it can, because the instructions give it the current list. No `accessCode` (3.4). No plate.

### 3.3 Output

```json
{ "state": "applied",                  // or "declined" when the person keeps things as they were
  "changed": [ { "field": "nozzle", "before": 0.4, "after": 0.6 } ],
  "printer": { "name": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.6, "nozzles": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
               "spools": [ ... ], "connected": false } }
```

The model reports only what `changed` says happened, then may suggest in its own words ("with 0.6 you can print thicker layers"). On "declined" it says nothing changed.

### 3.4 Access codes stay out of the model

A printer's LAN access code is a credential. Today the panel's placeholder asks the person to type it into the chat, which sends it to the model provider. In Add mode nothing receives it (the page never sends `accessCode`, and `printer_change` refuses in Add mode); in Change mode it passes through the model into this tool. Found by reading the code on `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`, not by running it.

Instead, the panel shows an access-code field on the network printer's card (Add) and in the Change panel for a printer that came from the network. The field sends the code straight to the app (`SetupCommands::set_printer_access_code`). The model may say "enter the access code in the field below" and never sees the code.

### 3.5 Confirmation

A change asks the person first, on a card that states it in words:

```
Change nozzle
0.4 mm → 0.6 mm on Bambu Lab A1 mini
Every project that uses this printer slices for 0.6 mm.
                              Keep 0.4 mm   [Set 0.6 mm]
```

For spools, the card lists the spools before and after. No tool name on the card. After "Set 0.6 mm", the app itself adds the line "Nozzle set to 0.6 mm" and an Undo button; it knows the old value, so the model is not asked to offer Undo.

### 3.6 Errors

| Code | When | Message carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nothing_to_change` | No field given | "Name the nozzle or the spools that changed" |
| `unknown_nozzle` | The size isn't one the model ships | The sizes it ships |
| `printer_gone` | The printer was renamed or removed while the card waited | The printer's name; "the panel has closed this printer" |

### 3.7 Side effects to remove (backend, not the tool's shape)

- **Changing a nozzle switches the open project's printer.** `Printers::change_named_printer_nozzle` selects the printer in the plater before saving (`J/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp`, around line 333, on `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`), and `settle_unsaved_changes` can raise OrcaSlicer's unsaved-changes dialog. Changing a printer from Home must not change what the open project prints on. Read from the code, not run.
- **Adding a printer marked the open project modified** in testing (F17 in `printer-panel-findings.md`). Probably the same cause.

### 3.8 Open for Kenneth

- **Whether a nozzle change should ask at all.** This design keeps the confirmation because the model is interpreting loose words ("i put a 0.6 on it") before a change that affects every project using the printer. The alternative is to apply it at once and rely on Undo.

---

## 4. Verification

- **Re-measure identification on the shipped model.** The spikes measured `gpt-5.6-terra` answering in JSON. The app is pinned to `gpt-5.4-mini` (`J/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp:58`) and answers through a tool call. Run both spike corpora (`spikes/printer-naming/corpus.jsonl`, `spikes/printer-photos/corpus.jsonl`) through the real tool path on `gpt-5.4-mini` before trusting this design. Add cases for "x1c", "voron 2.4 350mm", "prusa" (more than three fit), and "ender 3".
- **Record the footprint** per the tool guide (`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`): definition bytes for each mode's tool list, and input and cached tokens per request, for an Add and a Change conversation.
- **Update the tool guide.** It says every registered tool loads on every turn, lists no printer-panel exposure, and says no shipped tool skips the approval card. Record the printer session's per-mode tool list, the whole-list-in-the-prompt exception to "use bounded search" (with the spike as the evidence), and these two tools in the catalog record.
- **Tests:** each tool's input decoder (counts, unknown ids, nozzle sizes); the result carries no workspace; each mode offers only its tool; the access code never enters a tool input or the conversation; changing a nozzle leaves the open project's printer selection and modified flag untouched.

Researching `printer_change` turned up two problems that go beyond the tool's shape; they come first below, then the final design.

**Two problems found while researching `printer_change`** (from reading the code; I didn't run either):

- **Changing a nozzle from Home switches the open project to that printer**, and can pop up OrcaSlicer's unsaved-changes dialog.

**Final design**

The model does the understanding. The app does everything it already knows: drawing cards when you tap or browse, matching network printers, the Add and Undo buttons, and the "Browse the list · Set it up myself" buttons, which stay visible all the time. There are two tools, one per mode. Neither decides anything, and neither returns project data.

**`printer_identify` (adding a printer).** The model starts with the full printer list.
- **The model sends:** 1–3 printer ids, plus a nozzle size if one was mentioned. One id means it's sure; two or three mean it's asking. If more than three fit, or nothing fits, it asks or explains in words and doesn't call the tool.
- **The tool:** checks the ids and draws the cards.
- **The tool returns:** each printer's brand, model, size, nozzle sizes, what the app will assume, and whether you already own one. No approval step.

**`printer_change` (changing a printer).** The model starts knowing the printer's current nozzle, the sizes it supports, and its spools.
- **The model sends:** the new nozzle size and/or the full spool list.
- **The tool:** checks it, shows a confirmation card ("0.4 → 0.6 mm · Keep 0.4 / Set 0.6"), and saves.
- **The tool returns:** what changed, and the printer as it is now.

- Which filament to assume. The file's first choice for a Prusa MK3S is ABS, not PLA.
- Whether a nozzle change needs confirming at all.

content.text:
**Default filament: yes, there's a field for it — and the code reads the wrong one.** I've corrected the design doc.

- **The right field** is `default_filament_profile`, in each printer's per-nozzle profile file. For example, `Prusa MK3S 0.4 nozzle.json` says "Prusa Generic PLA", and `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle.json` says "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M". OrcaSlicer itself uses this field when you select a printer (`PresetBundle.cpp`). 893 of the 913 installable profiles have one, either directly or from the profile they inherit from.
- **What the code reads instead** is the first entry of `default_materials`. That's the list of filaments the setup wizard pre-ticks, not a default, and for the Prusa MK3S its first entry happens to be ABS.

So there's nothing for you to decide here: use OrcaSlicer's own field. I was wrong to frame it as an open question.

**"Confirm" means the approval card.** When the model decides to change the nozzle, the app shows a card ("0.4 mm → 0.6 mm · Keep 0.4 / Set 0.6") and changes nothing until you tap. The question is whether a nozzle change should skip the card and apply immediately.

**Keep the card:**
- **It catches misreadings.** The model is interpreting loose words. "I'm thinking of getting a 0.6", "put a 0.6 on the other one" and "I had a 0.6 once" could all be misread as a change.
- **It shows the consequence.** The change affects every project that uses this printer, and the card says so.
- **The tool guide requires it.** A change to a printer profile always needs approval, and the guide forbids the no-card exemption for anything that writes to disk or touches a printer. Skipping the card means changing the guide.
- **The cost:** one extra tap, and it can feel like the app doubts something you just told it. If cards appear too often, people start tapping through without reading.

**Skip the card, apply immediately, and offer Undo:**
- **It's more natural:** you say it, it's done.
- **A misreading takes effect silently.** You have to notice the "Nozzle set to 0.6 mm" line to catch it.
- **Undo isn't built,** and it has to reverse a saved profile change cleanly.
- **The tool guide would have to change.**

**My recommendation:** keep the card when the model is interpreting something you typed. When you tap a button that already names the exact change — such as Undo, which the app draws itself — apply it directly, because there's nothing to misread.
keep the card for typed changes, update the doc direclty in jusprin-newui repo, commit there, and push

### 2.6 Fix in the catalog: the wrong filament field

`PrinterCatalog.cpp` (around line 143) takes the first entry of the model file's `default_materials` and falls back to `default_filament_profile` only when that list is empty. `default_materials` is the list of filaments the setup wizard pre-ticks, not a default; for the Prusa MK3S its first entry is "Prusa Generic ABS". Read `default_filament_profile` from the machine preset for the chosen nozzle instead, and save and display that same value.

---

## 3. `printer_change`

### 3.1 What the model is told

At the start of every Change session, in the instructions, the printer as it is now:
- name, brand and model;
- current nozzle, **and the nozzle sizes this model ships**;
- the loaded spools as a list (name, material, colour), not a summary;
- whether it is connected.

Today the model gets a one-line summary and not the nozzle sizes, so it learns them only from an error.

The rules: work out what physically changed from what the person says. Change only what they said changed. The plate belongs to each project, not the printer; say where to change it and don't call the tool. A nozzle material (hardened steel) isn't tracked; say so. Connecting isn't possible from this panel.

Tool description:

> You work out what changed on this printer from what the person says. This tool checks it against what this printer's profile allows, asks the person to confirm, saves it, and returns the printer as it now is. It never decides what changed.

### 3.2 Input

```json
{ "nozzle": 0.6,                       // optional, mm
  "spools": [                          // optional; the complete list as it is now
    { "name": "Teal PLA", "material": "PLA", "colour": "#2a9d8f" } ] }
```

At least one field. `spools` replaces the whole list, so the model restates every spool; it can, because the instructions give it the current list. No `accessCode` (3.4). No plate.

### 3.3 Output

```json
{ "state": "applied",                  // or "declined" when the person keeps things as they were
  "changed": [ { "field": "nozzle", "before": 0.4, "after": 0.6 } ],
  "printer": { "name": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.6, "nozzles": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
               "spools": [ ... ], "connected": false } }
```

The model reports only what `changed` says happened, then may suggest in its own words ("with 0.6 you can print thicker layers"). On "declined" it says nothing changed.

### 3.4 Access codes stay out of the model

A printer's LAN access code is a credential. Today the panel's placeholder asks the person to type it into the chat, which sends it to the model provider. In Add mode nothing receives it (the page never sends `accessCode`, and `printer_change` refuses in Add mode); in Change mode it passes through the model into this tool. Found by reading the code on `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`, not by running it.

Instead, the panel shows an access-code field on the network printer's card (Add) and in the Change panel for a printer that came from the network. The field sends the code straight to the app (`SetupCommands::set_printer_access_code`). The model may say "enter the access code in the field below" and never sees the code.

### 3.5 Confirmation

A change asks the person first, on a card that states it in words:

```
Change nozzle
0.4 mm → 0.6 mm on Bambu Lab A1 mini
Every project that uses this printer slices for 0.6 mm.
                              Keep 0.4 mm   [Set 0.6 mm]
```

For spools, the card lists the spools before and after. No tool name on the card. After "Set 0.6 mm", the app itself adds the line "Nozzle set to 0.6 mm" and an Undo button; it knows the old value, so the model is not asked to offer Undo.

### 3.6 Errors

| Code | When | Message carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nothing_to_change` | No field given | "Name the nozzle or the spools that changed" |
| `unknown_nozzle` | The size isn't one the model ships | The sizes it ships |
| `printer_gone` | The printer was renamed or removed while the card waited | The printer's name; "the panel has closed this printer" |

### 3.7 Side effects to remove (backend, not the tool's shape)

- **Changing a nozzle switches the open project's printer.** `Printers::change_named_printer_nozzle` selects the printer in the plater before saving (`J/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp`, around line 333, on `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`), and `settle_unsaved_changes` can raise OrcaSlicer's unsaved-changes dialog. Changing a printer from Home must not change what the open project prints on. Read from the code, not run.
- **Adding a printer marked the open project modified** in testing (F17 in `printer-panel-findings.md`). Probably the same cause.

### 3.8 Open for Kenneth

- **Whether a nozzle change should ask at all.** This design keeps the confirmation because the model is interpreting loose words ("i put a 0.6 on it") before a change that affects every project using the printer. The alternative is to apply it at once and rely on Undo.

---

## 4. Verification

- **Re-measure identification on the shipped model.** The spikes measured `gpt-5.6-terra` answering in JSON. The app is pinned to `gpt-5.4-mini` (`J/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp:58`) and answers through a tool call. Run both spike corpora (`spikes/printer-naming/corpus.jsonl`, `spikes/printer-photos/corpus.jsonl`) through the real tool path on `gpt-5.4-mini` before trusting this design. Add cases for "x1c", "voron 2.4 350mm", "prusa" (more than three fit), and "ender 3".
- **Record the footprint** per the tool guide (`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`): definition bytes for each mode's tool list, and input and cached tokens per request, for an Add and a Change conversation.
- **Update the tool guide.** It says every registered tool loads on every turn, lists no printer-panel exposure, and says no shipped tool skips the approval card. Record the printer session's per-mode tool list, the whole-list-in-the-prompt exception to "use bounded search" (with the spike as the evidence), and these two tools in the catalog record.
- **Tests:** each tool's input decoder (counts, unknown ids, nozzle sizes); the result carries no workspace; each mode offers only its tool; the access code never enters a tool input or the conversation; changing a nozzle leaves the open project's printer selection and modified flag untouched.

The printer panel on Home lets a person add a printer or change one they
have by talking to the in-app agent. The first build gave the agent four

model relayed. This records the replacement: the model does the

nozzle and/or the full spool list, confirms on a card that states the
change in words, saves it and returns what changed. Neither returns the
open project's workspace; access codes never pass through the model.

Also records two catalog facts found while designing: the app reads the
wizard's pre-ticked filament list instead of OrcaSlicer's own
default_filament_profile, and only 34 of 359 printer models say which
plate they ship with. Kenneth's decision on confirmation is in 3.5: typed
changes always show the card; an app button that names the exact change,
such as Undo, applies directly.

EOF

# Handoff: how the model and the app share the printer flow

Status: decided by Kenneth, 2026-09-18. Not built. This document replaces the earlier version of this file (commit `f4a3920443`) and, for everything between the model and the app, the WP1 section of `printer-panel-fixes-handoff.md` on branch `printer-conversation-panel-with-stupid-wp1-wpx`.

Scope: only how the in-app model and the app divide the printer flow — what the model is told, which tools it has, what they take and return, and what the app tells the model. Screen layout is out of scope; where this document says "the app draws", the drawing itself follows the existing wireframes.

Paths are relative to the repo root. `J/` is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

---

## 1. Starting point, and what is wrong with it

Build from branch `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb` at commit `0e55c4f9be`. That commit put an agent conversation in Home's printers column, for adding a printer and for changing one. Its model–app split is backwards:

- **The app orders the model to call tools.** After the person taps "This one", the app sends the model "Propose that printer alone with printer_propose and say in one sentence what you assumed" (`J/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`, around line 561). After "Use this" on a network printer, it sends "Find that model with printer_catalog_search, propose it…" (around line 548). The app already knows the answer in both cases; the model only relays it.
- **Tools carry the model's wording, not facts.** `printer_suggest` exists to draw buttons whose labels the model writes, and the instructions script some of those labels.
- **The printer is found by keyword filter.** `printer_catalog_search` keeps a model only when every word of the query appears in its name, returns the first few in file order, and gives no count. In testing, "voron 2.4 350mm" was reported unsupported, "x1c" matched another manufacturer's printer, and "prusa" showed three of thirteen Prusa models as if they were all.
- **Every tool result carries the open project.** `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` (`J/Agent/AgentHost.cpp`, around line 1836) adds the whole project workspace to every result, although a printer conversation has nothing to do with the project.
- **Access codes go through the model.** The panel asks the person to type a printer's access code into the chat, which sends it to the model provider.

## 2. The rule

**The model does the understanding. If the app can work something out without the model, the app does it.**

- The model works out which printer someone has from their words or photo, and what changed on a printer they own. It asks when unsure, and it explains, answers and suggests in its own words.
- A tool checks the model's decision against the real printer data, carries it out, and returns facts the model needs for its next sentence. A tool never decides, and never carries the model's wording.
- The app handles every tap whose result it already knows. Afterwards it records what happened in the conversation as a plain statement, so the model can answer follow-ups. **The app never tells the model what to do or which tool to call.**

## 3. Who handles what

| The person… | Handled by | What the model sees afterwards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Types a printer, or sends a photo of it | **Model**, then `printer_identify` | Its own call and the tool's result |
| Describes something that fits more than three printers ("ender 3") | **Model**, in words: one narrowing question and where to look, or "Browse the list" | — (no tool call) |
| Describes a printer that isn't in the list, or a resin/laser machine | **Model**, in words | — (no tool call) |
| Taps "This one" on a candidate card | **App** draws that printer's card with its assumptions | Event: `The person chose Prusa MK3S. Its card offers Add, assuming a 0.4 mm nozzle and Prusa Generic PLA; the profile names no plate.` No model turn. |
| Picks a printer from "Browse the list" | **App**, as above | Event, as above. No model turn. |
| Taps "Use this" on a printer found on the network | **App** matches it by the model id the printer reports and draws its card with the reported facts | Event: `The person chose the network printer 01P00A3B, a Bambu Lab A1 mini that reports a 0.4 mm nozzle.` No model turn. If the reported model id matches nothing in the list, the app records that and starts a model turn so the model can ask. |
| Taps "Not this one" | **App** collapses the card and clears the pinned card | Event: `The person said Bambu Lab A1 mini is not their printer.` **Starts a model turn**: the model decides what to ask next. |
| Taps "Add this printer" | **App** saves it and closes the panel | Nothing (the conversation ends) |
| Taps "Set it up myself" or "Browse the list" | **App** | Nothing |
| Enters an access code | **App**, through its own field, straight to `SetupCommands::set_printer_access_code` | Event: `An access code was entered.` Never the code. |
| Types a change to a printer they own ("i put a 0.6 nozzle on it") | **Model**, then `printer_change`, which asks the person to confirm on a card | Its own call and the tool's result |
| Taps Undo after a change | **App** reverses it directly, with no card | Event: `The person undid the change: the nozzle is 0.4 mm again.` No model turn. |
| Mentions the plate, or a nozzle material ("hardened steel") | **Model**, in words: the plate belongs to each project, and nozzle material isn't tracked | — (no tool call) |
| Asks to connect the printer, or for network setup help | **Model**, in one sentence: it can't do that from this panel | — (no tool call) |

## 4. Session setup

Every opening of the panel is a new conversation. Each mode offers **exactly one tool**. No project data enters the conversation: not in the instructions, not in tool results.

### 4.1 Add mode

- **Tool:** `printer_identify` only.
- **Instructions:** the rules in 5.1, then the whole printer list, one line per model:

  ```
  <catalogId> | <brand> <model> | <build volume>
  BBL/N1 | Bambu Lab A1 mini | 180 × 180 × 180 mm
  Prusa/MK3S | Prusa MK3S | 250 × 210 × 210 mm
  ```

  The name column is required. The app's catalog ids join the brand folder and the profile's `model_id`, which is often opaque (`N1` is the A1 mini, `BL-P001` the X1 Carbon); without the name the model cannot match what people say. Build the list from `PrinterCatalog` (`J/PrinterSetup/PrinterCatalog.cpp`), leaving out the Orca Arena bundle (`resources/profiles/OrcaArena.json`, decided 2026-09-17). About 384 lines; measure the tokens (section 8).

### 4.2 Change mode

- **Tool:** `printer_change` only.
- **Instructions:** the rules in 6.1, then the printer as it is now: name, brand and model; current nozzle and **every nozzle size this model ships**; the loaded spools as a list (name, material, colour); whether it is connected.

## 5. `printer_identify`

### 5.1 Instructions (rules)

Adapted from `agent-docs/jusprin/spikes/printer-naming/instructions.v2.txt` and `spikes/printer-photos/instructions.v2.txt` (on branch `printer-conversation-panel-with-stupid-wp1-wpx`):

- One printer fits: call the tool with it.
- Two or three genuinely fit: call the tool with all of them, and ask in your reply what tells them apart.
- More than three fit: do not call the tool. Ask one question that narrows it down and say where to look, or point to "Browse the list". Never show three of many.
- A query that is the start of more than one model name is not a clear match, even when it exactly equals one of them.
- Nothing fits, or it isn't a filament printer: say so in one sentence; do not call the tool.
- A photo: name a model only from a readable name or a printed size. Going by shape alone, ask for a photo of the label (a sticker on the back, a plate under the frame, the About page on the screen). Never quote a label as read unless asking the person to confirm it. Never judge size from how big it looks. A clone uses the profile of the model it copies.
- Write every reply from the facts the tool returns, never from memory.

### 5.2 Description (verbatim)

> You decide which printer this is. This tool checks the printers you name against the app's printer list, shows them to the person, and returns the details to mention. It never picks a printer.

### 5.3 Input

```json
{ "catalogIds": ["Prusa/MK3S"],   // 1 to 3, copied exactly from the printer list
  "nozzle": 0.6 }                  // optional, mm; only when the person or a photo said so
```

Nothing else. The count carries the model's certainty: one id means sure, and the card offers "Add this printer"; two or three mean unsure, and each card offers "This one".

### 5.4 Output (JSON)

```json
{ "printers": [
    { "catalogId": "Prusa/MK3S",
      "brand": "Prusa",
      "model": "MK3S",
      "buildVolume": "250 × 210 × 210 mm",
      "nozzles": [0.25, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
      "assumed": { "nozzle": 0.4, "plate": null, "filament": "Prusa Generic PLA" },
      "alreadyYours": false } ] }
```

| Field | Where the app gets it |
| --- | --- |
| `brand` | `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json`, its `name` |
| `model` | The model's profile name with the brand not repeated |
| `buildVolume` | The machine preset's `printable_area` and `printable_height`, following `inherits` |
| `nozzles` | The model file's `nozzle_diameter` |
| `assumed.nozzle` | The nozzle the model passed; else 0.4 when the model ships it; else its first size |
| `assumed.plate` | The model file's `default_bed_type`. **`null` when absent**, which is most printers (34 of 359 model files have one) |
| `assumed.filament` | The machine preset's `default_filament_profile` for that nozzle size, following `inherits`. This is OrcaSlicer's own default. Not the first entry of `default_materials`, which is the wizard's pre-ticked list (see 7) |
| `alreadyYours` | Whether a saved printer is this model |

JSON, not prose, because `null` tells the model there is nothing to say (prose leaves a gap the model fills), values are quotable exactly, and the result can be checked and tested like every other tool in the app.

### 5.5 Errors

| Code | When | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unknown_printer` | An id is not on the list | Names the id; "copy it exactly from the printer list" |
| `too_many` | More than three ids | "More than three fit. Ask one question that narrows it down instead." |
| `unknown_nozzle` | The nozzle isn't one the model ships | Lists the sizes it ships |

### 5.6 Approval

None. The tool saves nothing; the person's tap on "Add this printer" is the decision.

### 5.7 Worked examples (acceptance cases)

**"the small bambu one"**
1. The model, from the list and its knowledge, settles on the A1 mini, and calls `{"catalogIds": ["BBL/N1"]}`.
2. The result gives the A1 mini: 180 × 180 × 180 mm; nozzles 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8; assumed 0.4 mm, Textured PEI Plate, Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M.
3. The model replies from those facts: "That's the Bambu Lab A1 mini. I'll assume the 0.4 mm nozzle, the Textured PEI plate and Bambu PLA Basic — change any of them here or in your first project."

**"voron 2.4 350mm"**
The model reads "350mm" as the 350 size and calls `{"catalogIds": ["Voron/Voron2_350"]}`. The result has `"plate": null`, so the reply says nothing about a plate. No word matching happens anywhere.

**"ender 3"**
Twelve models begin "Ender-3". The model does not call the tool; it asks which one and says the version is on the front label, or offers "Browse the list".

**"the prusa, the 0.3 nozzle"**
The model calls `{"catalogIds": ["Prusa/MK3S"], "nozzle": 0.3}`, gets `unknown_nozzle` listing 0.25, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8, and asks which one it is.

**"my elegoo mars"**
Not a filament printer. The model says so in one sentence; no tool call.

## 6. `printer_change`

### 6.1 Instructions (rules)

- Work out what physically changed from what the person says; change only that.
- The plate belongs to each project, not the printer: say where to change it; no tool call.
- Nozzle material isn't tracked: say so; no tool call.
- Connecting a printer isn't possible from this panel: say so in one sentence.
- Report only what the tool's result says changed.

### 6.2 Description (verbatim)

> You work out what changed on this printer from what the person says. This tool checks it against what this printer's profile allows, asks the person to confirm, saves it, and returns the printer as it now is. It never decides what changed.

### 6.3 Input

```json
{ "nozzle": 0.6,                     // optional, mm
  "spools": [                        // optional; the complete list as it is now
    { "name": "Teal PLA", "material": "PLA", "colour": "#2a9d8f" } ] }
```

At least one field. `spools` replaces the whole list; the model can restate it because its instructions carry the current list. No access code, no plate.

### 6.4 Confirmation (Kenneth, 2026-09-18)

- **Every call from the model shows a card** before anything is saved, stating the change in words:

  ```
  Change nozzle
  0.4 mm → 0.6 mm on Bambu Lab A1 mini
  Every project that uses this printer slices for 0.6 mm.
                                Keep 0.4 mm   [Set 0.6 mm]
  ```

  For spools, the card lists them before and after. No tool name on the card. The model is interpreting loose words ("i put a 0.6 on it", "I'm thinking of a 0.6"), and the change affects every project on that printer; the card is where a misreading is caught.
- **Undo is the app's, not the model's.** After a change the app adds "Nozzle set to 0.6 mm · Undo". Undo names the exact change, so it applies directly, through the same backend operation, without a card and without the model.

### 6.5 Output (JSON)

```json
{ "state": "applied",                // or "declined" when the person taps "Keep 0.4 mm"
  "changed": [ { "field": "nozzle", "before": 0.4, "after": 0.6 } ],
  "printer": { "name": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.6, "nozzles": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
               "spools": [ ], "connected": false } }
```

The model states only what `changed` says happened, then may add its own advice ("with 0.6 you can print thicker layers"). On `declined` it says nothing changed.

### 6.6 Errors

| Code | When | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nothing_to_change` | No field given | "Name the nozzle or the spools that changed." |
| `unknown_nozzle` | The size isn't one the model ships | Lists the sizes it ships |
| `printer_gone` | The printer was renamed or removed while the card waited | Names the printer |

### 6.7 Worked examples (acceptance cases)

**"i put a 0.6 nozzle on it"** (A1 mini) → `{"nozzle": 0.6}` → card → "Set 0.6 mm" → `applied`, changed 0.4 → 0.6 → "Done — it's on the 0.6 mm nozzle now. You can print thicker layers with it."

**"swapped to a hardened steel 0.4"** → no call: "The size is still 0.4 mm, so nothing changes here; the app doesn't track nozzle material."

**"the plate is smooth PEI now"** → no call: the plate is chosen per project, in the project's printer menu.

**"i put a 0.3 on it"** → `{"nozzle": 0.3}` → `unknown_nozzle` listing 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 → the model asks which it is.

## 7. What the app tells the model: events

The app records its own actions as **events**: one plain sentence each, stating what happened (examples in section 3). Rules:

- **Statements, never instructions.** "The person chose Prusa MK3S", never "Propose Prusa MK3S".
- **Events must reach the model.** Today the only way the app writes to the thread is a note (`AgentHost::post_note`), and notes are deliberately left out of the model's context (`J/Agent/AgentHost.cpp`, around line 1608: "Notes stay out of the model's context"). Events need to be in the model's context on its next turn. Add an event kind for the printer session that the history includes, or include notes in that session only; either way, test it.
- **Most events start no model turn.** Only "Not this one", and a network printer the app cannot match, start one, because only then does the person need the model's next words.
- The conversation history kept for the model is capped at 20 messages today (`kHistoryMessages`). Count events against it or not, but decide deliberately.

## 8. What to remove from `0e55c4f9be`

- `printer_catalog_search`, `printer_propose`, `printer_suggest` from the registry (`J/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, around line 1432), and `OrcaPrinterBackend::search_catalog`.
- Every `ask_agent` prompt that tells the model what to call (`J/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`).
- Scripted button labels in the instructions.
- The `planId` field the registry adds to every change tool (`joins_plans`, `J/Agent/ToolRegistry.hpp`): neither printer tool joins grouped approvals.
- The project workspace in printer tool results.
- `accessCode` from `printer_change`, and the "access code, optional" placeholder that asks for it in the chat.
- `say`, `question`, `action`, `reason`, `plate`, `filament` and `provenance` inputs from any identify tool.

## 9. Back-end fixes this design depends on

- **Per-session tool lists by mode:** Add offers only `printer_identify`, Change only `printer_change`. Offering every tool in both modes lets a Change conversation call the identify tool and clear the pinned card of an existing printer.
- **Default filament from the right field.** `PrinterCatalog.cpp` (around line 143) takes the first entry of `default_materials` and falls back to `default_filament_profile` only when that list is empty. For the Prusa MK3S that yields "Prusa Generic ABS". Read `default_filament_profile` for the chosen nozzle, and save and show that same value.
- **Plate unknown is `null`,** never a guess.
- **A nozzle change must not touch the open project.** On the fix branch, `Printers::change_named_printer_nozzle` selects the printer in the plater before saving and can raise OrcaSlicer's unsaved-changes dialog (`J/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp`, around line 333, branch `printer-conversation-panel-with-stupid-wp1-wpx`; read, not run). Changing a printer from Home must leave the project's printer selection and modified flag alone.
- **Events in the model's context** (section 7).

## 10. Verification

- **Re-measure identification on the model the app ships.** The spikes measured `gpt-5.6-terra` answering in JSON. The app is pinned to `gpt-5.4-mini` (`J/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp:58`) and answers through a tool call. Run both spike test sets through the real tool path on `gpt-5.4-mini`, plus the cases that failed in testing: "x1c", "voron 2.4 350mm", "prusa", "ender 3".
- **The worked examples in 5.7 and 6.7 pass** in the built app with the live agent.
- **Unit tests:**
  - each tool's input checks (id counts, unknown ids, nozzle sizes);
  - results carry no workspace;
  - each mode offers only its own tool;
  - no event is an instruction, and events reach the model's context;
  - no access code enters a tool input or the conversation;
  - a nozzle change leaves the open project's selection and modified flag untouched;
  - Undo applies without a card.
- **Measure the footprint** as the tool guide requires (`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`): definition bytes per mode, and input and cached tokens per request, for an Add and a Change conversation.
- **Update the tool guide:** the printer session's per-mode tool list; the whole-list-in-the-prompt exception to "use bounded search", with the spike as evidence; both tools in the catalog record.

## 11. Decisions (Kenneth)

- 2026-09-17: the real in-app agent handles adding and changing printers; the Orca Arena bundle is hidden from the add-printer flow only (still in the wizard); no agent set up means the agent-setup page.
- 2026-09-18: two tools, one per mode, as specified here; a change the model works out from typed words always shows the confirmation card; Undo applies directly.

## 12. Open questions

1	# Handoff: how the model and the app share the printer flow
2	
3	Status: decided by Kenneth, 2026-09-18. Not built. This document replaces the earlier version of this file (commit `f4a3920443`). Build only from this document and branch `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb`; no other branch or handoff applies.
4	
5	Scope: only how the in-app model and the app divide the printer flow — what the model is told, which tools it has, what they take and return, and what the app tells the model. Screen layout is out of scope; where this document says "the app draws", the drawing itself follows the existing wireframes.
6	
7	Paths are relative to the repo root. `J/` is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Starting point, and what is wrong with it
12	
13	Build from branch `claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb` at commit `0e55c4f9be`. That commit put an agent conversation in Home's printers column, for adding a printer and for changing one. Its model–app split is backwards:
14	
15	- **The app orders the model to call tools.** After the person taps "This one", the app sends the model "Propose that printer alone with printer_propose and say in one sentence what you assumed" (`J/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`, around line 561). After "Use this" on a network printer, it sends "Find that model with printer_catalog_search, propose it…" (around line 548). The app already knows the answer in both cases; the model only relays it.
16	- **Tools carry the model's wording, not facts.** `printer_suggest` exists to draw buttons whose labels the model writes, and the instructions script some of those labels.
17	- **The printer is found by keyword filter.** `printer_catalog_search` keeps a model only when every word of the query appears in its name, returns the first few in file order, and gives no count. In testing, "voron 2.4 350mm" was reported unsupported, "x1c" matched another manufacturer's printer, and "prusa" showed three of thirteen Prusa models as if they were all.
18	- **Every tool result carries the open project.** `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` (`J/Agent/AgentHost.cpp`, around line 1797) adds the whole project workspace to every result, although a printer conversation has nothing to do with the project.
19	- **Access codes go through the model.** The panel asks the person to type a printer's access code into the chat, which sends it to the model provider.
20	
21	## 2. The rule
22	
23	**The model does the understanding. If the app can work something out without the model, the app does it.**
24	
25	- The model works out which printer someone has from their words or photo, and what changed on a printer they own. It asks when unsure, and it explains, answers and suggests in its own words.
26	- A tool checks the model's decision against the real printer data, carries it out, and returns facts the model needs for its next sentence. A tool never decides, and never carries the model's wording.
27	- The app handles every tap whose result it already knows. Afterwards it records what happened in the conversation as a plain statement, so the model can answer follow-ups. **The app never tells the model what to do or which tool to call.**
28	
29	## 3. Who handles what
30	
31	| The person… | Handled by | What the model sees afterwards |
32	| --- | --- | --- |
33	| Types a printer, or sends a photo of it | **Model**, then `printer_identify` | Its own call and the tool's result |
34	| Describes something that fits more than three printers ("ender 3") | **Model**, in words: one narrowing question and where to look, or "Browse the list" | — (no tool call) |
35	| Describes a printer that isn't in the list, or a resin/laser machine | **Model**, in words | — (no tool call) |
36	| Taps "This one" on a candidate card | **App** draws that printer's card with its assumptions | Event: `The person chose Prusa MK3S. Its card offers Add, assuming a 0.4 mm nozzle and Prusa Generic PLA; the profile names no plate.` No model turn. |
37	| Picks a printer from "Browse the list" | **App**, as above | Event, as above. No model turn. |
38	| Taps "Use this" on a printer found on the network | **App** matches it by the model id the printer reports and draws its card with the reported facts | Event: `The person chose the network printer 01P00A3B, a Bambu Lab A1 mini that reports a 0.4 mm nozzle.` No model turn. If the reported model id matches nothing in the list, the app records that and starts a model turn so the model can ask. |
39	| Taps "Not this one" | **App** collapses the card and clears the pinned card | Event: `The person said Bambu Lab A1 mini is not their printer.` **Starts a model turn**: the model decides what to ask next. |
40	| Taps "Add this printer" | **App** saves it and closes the panel | Nothing (the conversation ends) |
41	| Taps "Set it up myself" or "Browse the list" | **App** | Nothing |
42	| Enters an access code | **App**, through its own field, straight to `SetupCommands::set_printer_access_code` | Event: `An access code was entered.` Never the code. |
43	| Types a change to a printer they own ("i put a 0.6 nozzle on it") | **Model**, then `printer_change`, which asks the person to confirm on a card | Its own call and the tool's result |
44	| Taps Undo after a change | **App** reverses it directly, with no card | Event: `The person undid the change: the nozzle is 0.4 mm again.` No model turn. |
45	| Mentions the plate, or a nozzle material ("hardened steel") | **Model**, in words: the plate belongs to each project, and nozzle material isn't tracked | — (no tool call) |
46	| Asks to connect the printer, or for network setup help | **Model**, in one sentence: it can't do that from this panel | — (no tool call) |
47	
48	## 4. Session setup
49	
50	Every opening of the panel is a new conversation. Each mode offers **exactly one tool**. No project data enters the conversation: not in the instructions, not in tool results.
51	
52	### 4.1 Add mode
53	
54	- **Tool:** `printer_identify` only.
55	- **Instructions:** the rules in 5.1, then the whole printer list, one line per model:
56	
57	  ```
58	  <catalogId> | <brand> <model> | <build volume>
59	  BBL/N1 | Bambu Lab A1 mini | 180 × 180 × 180 mm
60	  Prusa/MK3S | Prusa MK3S | 250 × 210 × 210 mm
61	  ```
62	
63	  The name column is required. The app's catalog ids join the brand folder and the profile's `model_id`, which is often opaque (`N1` is the A1 mini, `BL-P001` the X1 Carbon); without the name the model cannot match what people say. Build the list from `PrinterCatalog` (`J/PrinterSetup/PrinterCatalog.cpp`), leaving out the Orca Arena bundle (`resources/profiles/OrcaArena.json`, decided 2026-09-17). About 384 lines; measure the tokens (section 10).
64	
65	### 4.2 Change mode
66	
67	- **Tool:** `printer_change` only.
68	- **Instructions:** the rules in 6.1, then the printer as it is now: name, brand and model; current nozzle and **every nozzle size this model ships**; the loaded spools as a list (name, material, colour); whether it is connected.
